#2629. Tresoldi lascia la Germania Under 21: niente Belgio dopo il trauma cranico

Lo staff medico ha fermato per precauzione anche Hendry Blank e ha autorizzato entrambi a tornare ai rispettivi club.

Nicolò Tresoldi salterà la sfida della Germania Under 21 contro il Belgio e tornerà al Bruges dopo aver riportato un trauma cranico in nazionale. Secondo quanto riportato da SportMediaset, L’attaccante si è scontrato testa contro testa con il compagno Hendry Blank durante la rifinitura.

#2628. How does Seattle Seahawks’ offense look with Drew Lock at quarterback for Week 10 matchup against Las Vegas Raiders?

Week 10 features an old-school AFC West rivalry as the then-Oakland, now Las Vegas Raiders and Seattle Seahawks had plenty of noteworthy divisional battles in the '80s and '90s before the NFL's realignment that pushed Seattle into the NFC. To preview this weekend's matchup, Silver and Black Pride reached out to our friends at Field Gulls, and John Gilbert was kind enough to answer a few questions about the Seahawks for Raider Nation.

Q: Sam Darnold has already been ruled out, meaning Drew Lock will make his fourth appearance and third start this season. What's the difference in the Seahawks' offense with Lock at quarterback, and what's the fanbase's confidence level in him as the starter?

A: In years past, the answer to this would hark back to Pete Carroll's 2023 comments about Lock making a couple of boneheaded throws. But when Lock has played this season, he has done a phenomenal job protecting the football.

Darnold has missed two full games and only played five snaps in the season opener against the New England Patriots. Yet in spite of that, he is tied with Matthew Stafford for the most interceptions thrown in the NFC.

On the flip side, Lock has five touchdowns and no interceptions while starting twice and playing most of the game against the Patriots. Of course, both of Lock's starts came against the Arizona Cardinals, and the Arizona defense has done a solid job helping opposing quarterbacks bolster their stat lines this season, so we'll see what Lock can do against the Raiders.

Q: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is coming off a season where he led the NFL with nearly 1,800 receiving yards and won Offensive Player of the Year. So far in 2026, he's the first and currently only player to eclipse the 1,000-yard mark while averaging about 10 yards per game more than he did last year. What makes JSN such a tough cover? Any suggestions for how to keep him in check?

A: JSN has simply become a monster. He's a very smooth and fluid route runner, and at the foundation of his greatness is the simple fact that all of his route stems look the same, making it impossible for defensive backs to anticipate what is coming.

Add in great hands, a phenomenal work ethic and the reality that he is far and away the most dangerous offensive weapon in the Seattle arsenal. It's a recipe to continue to feed him the ball until defenses can find a way to slow him down.

Teams have tried almost everything to slow JSN down, but a consistent weakness has not yet been found. Jamming him at the line doesn't stop him. Bracketing doesn't stop him. Whatever opponents do, he just continues to find ways to get open and keep the offense moving.

Q: Seattle's rushing attack ranks 18th in yards per game, 25th in yards per carry and 27th in EPA per rush, according to Sumer Sports. Are the issues as simple as the offense missing Klint Kubiak and Kenneth Walker III? Has adding Quenton Nelson helped at all?

A: Losing Kenneth Walker III to the Chiefs in free agency certainly hurt. The two biggest things the Seattle run game has missed for most of the first half of the season were the explosiveness and the ball security that Walker brought to the table.

Yes, he had a style that could be infuriating at times, as he had a tendency to try to bounce so many runs outside looking for the big play. But the simple fact is that he has the burst and speed to create an outsized number of explosive plays, even while consistently finishing in the bottom half of the league in success rate.

During his four seasons in Seattle, Walker fumbled a total of three times on 821 regular-season rushing attempts, while his replacements (Jadarian Price, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani) have put the ball on the ground six times in 195 rushing attempts so far this season.

With that said, Zach Charbonnet is back in the lineup after tearing his ACL in the 2025 postseason, and his presence has been an instant upgrade at the position. Charbonnet is never going to present the big-play threat that Walker brought to the field on every rushing attempt, but Charbonnet is a disciplined back who will follow his blocking, while providing solid pass protection from the backfield in passing situations.

As for Quenton Nelson, so far the trade has produced more excitement and hype than on-field production. Nelson apparently suffered a minor knee injury before the trade and had a procedure to address the issue. As such, with the Seahawks enjoying a bye week after facing off against the Raiders, he likely won't be back in action again until Week 12 against the San Francisco 49ers.

Q: Imagine you're Kubiak game-planning for Fernando Mendoza's first start against the vaunted Seahawks' defense. How would you attack the defense and give the rookie quarterback his best chance at having success? Keep in mind that the Raiders are one of the few teams that are worse at running the ball than the Seahawks are.

A: Where Kubiak really seemed to excel in Seattle was creating tendencies, or the appearance of tendencies, and then in high-leverage situations making it look like the offense is following that tendency, only to break off for a big play.

So, whatever tendencies the Raiders offense has put on tape through the first half of the season, I expect those tendencies to be thrown out the window at key times within the games as Kubiak looks for big plays.

The reality is that while the Seahawks defense is great, so far in 2026 the Seahawks offense hasn't shown to be on par with the 2025 group, and between conservative playcalling and Drew Lock battling oblique and elbow issues, it might only take a couple of big plays for the Raiders to play spoilers against the defending champs.

Q: Between Leonard Williams, Byron Murphy II, Devon Witherspoon, Ernest Jones IV and Nick Emmanwori, Seattle's defense is filled with studs. If you had to pick one to deem the biggest key or X-factor for the unit, who would it be and why?

A: As cliché as it sounds, there is no one piece that makes the defense tick. What makes Mike Macdonald's defenses so good is that all eleven players are on the same page, doing their jobs at a high level. All of the big names on defense play key roles, but as a whole the group has enough depth that a single missing piece doesn't send things off the rails.

With that all said, everything starts in the trenches. So if Williams and Murphy aren't able to do their thing up front, it leaves the rest of the defense hanging.

#2627. Jared Goff takes 1-3 career record vs. Patriots into Germany game

For his career, Lions quarterback Jared Goff has a record of 101-67-1 as a starter. That’s a 59.7-percent win rate.

Against the Patriots, Goff is 1-3. That’s a 25-percent win rate.

In those four games, Goff has two touchdown passes and five interceptions.

Sunday’s game in Germany will be the first one against the Patriots with a coach other than Bill Belichick. Goff has never faced current Patriots coach Mike Vrabel; during Goff’s time as a starter with the Rams and Lions and Vrabel’s tenure with the Titans, their two teams never crossed paths.

Goff’s first loss to New England came in 2016, in his third career start. The Patriots won, 26-10. Two years later, New England beat Goff and the Rams in the Super Bowl, 13-3.

In 2020, Goff and the Rams beat the Patriots, 24-3. In 2022, the Patriots beat Goff and the Lions, 29-0.

Sunday’s game is consequential for both teams. The 6-2 Lions are caught in a cluster of four NFC North teams that all have six or more wins. The Patriots, at 5-4, are fading in the AFC East race and could be scrambling to secure a wild-card spot.

#2626. Jared Curtis, Junior Sherrill injury updates after Vanderbilt football vs Alabama

Junior Sherrill, Vanderbilt football's leading wide receiver, went down after a third-down play with 1:53 left in its Nov. 14 game against Alabama at FirstBank Stadium and hobbled off the field with the apparent injury.

Quarterback Jared Curtis also took a big hit that led to him going into the injury tent, though he ultimately finished the game.

The Commodores were down 21-6 at the time, which ended up being the final score of the game.

Sherrill is likely to be fine, coach Clark Lea said after the game, and the injury was a cramp. Curtis will be examined further to make sure there is nothing serious.

"Junior's fine," Lea said. "He was a cramp, and so we will evaluate him to make sure he's OK. But I don't suspect that to be anything. ... I don't have all the specifics on the hit (Curtis) took early, but he was able to go to the tent, get it sorted out. He was able to finish the game without issue. Now, we'll need further examination to make sure that there's nothing there."

Sherrill had seven catches for 100 yards in the game, including one 44-yard catch. This season, he has 63 catches for 847 yards.

Vanderbilt (4-6, 2-6 SEC) will next travel to Gainesville to face Florida at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium on Nov. 21 (11 a.m. CT, TV network TBD).

#2625. Steelers will have backup referee for matchup vs. Bengals

The Pittsburgh Steelers are set to take on the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football for sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Whoever comes out of Paycor Stadium with a victory on primetime will have the inside track to win the division.

With the stakes as high as they are, an underrated storyline in the contest is how the Friday mandatory ground stop on Friday will impact the referee crew for the Steelers vs. Bengals showdown.

Longtime side judge Don Willard is working an unprecedented schedule due to travel problems. He will serve as the head referee for the Colts matchup against the Dolphins in Indianapolis on at 1 pm. After the conclusion of that game, Willard will make the drive to Cincinnati for Sunday Night Football, where he will also serve as the head referee.

The usual crew that Willard usually works with is not scheduled to work at all this weekend. The longtime side judge will step into a major role for two separate games on Sunday.

While the league has had to make major changes to officiating crews for Sunday, it does not seem that the ground stoppage will have a major effect on any teams travels plans. Last night, Steelers director of communications Burt Lauten suggested that the team was considering bussing to Cincinnati. At the time of this writing, there is no update as to whether the Steelers will fly or drive to Cincinnati after the ground stoppage was lifted late last night.

#2624. Bucks vs. Magic Player Grades: Bigs peform, team forgets how to make free throws

The Milwaukee Bucks fall out of NBA Cup contention, losing 107-99 against the Orlando Magic in an improved effort. The Bucks allowed the Magic to build a double-digit lead after a poor first half, but they kept battling and won the final two quarters. Yet again, the Bucks went on multiple long stretches where they couldn't score, which wasn't helped by their 58% combined shooting from the charity stripe. Overall, there were some positives to take from this game, but it was another incomplete effort. Read our full summary of the game here and catch a six-minute audio recap on the Bucks+ podcast, Bucks In Six Minutes, below.

29 minutes, 8 points, 10 rebounds, 2 assists, 3 turnovers, 3/8 FG, 0/4 3P, -4

It wasn't the offensive night Rollins wanted, but his rebounding made up for that. The way he stuck his nose in there and finished possessions was a huge reason the Bucks were able to stay in the game. I thought his defence was really solid too. Also, Rollins played nearly 30 minutes. Yay!

34 minutes, 18 points, 1 rebound, 2 assists, 2 steals, 1 block, 5/17 FG, 2/7 3P, 6/7 FT, -1

The Magic's big, physical guards did an excellent job making Herro work for absolutely everything, and he looked really worn down as the game went on. Fair or unfair, the Bucks need more from Herro to have a chance to win; 5/17 isn't good enough. I do want to credit him for his impact on the defensive end, though; don't get me wrong, the Magic still went at Herro, but he found a way to make a difference with three stocks.

28 minutes, 22 points, 6 rebounds, 4 assists, 2 turnovers, 8/15 FG, 5/7 3P, 1/3 FT, -3

Another great game off the bench for Jaquez. It really feels like he's come into this season realising that, to get to the next level, he has to take and make threes at a higher clip; he's currently shooting 40.4% on 4.3 attempts per game—both career highs by a mile. Five of Jaquez's eight makes against the Magic were from three, so he could have really gone crazy if his middle game was working.

30 minutes, 14 points, 4 rebounds, 2 assists, 2 steals, 1 block, 3 turnovers, 3/9 FG, 1/5 3P, 7/15 FT, -2

I'm sorry, he did some good things, but this was way too much Kuzma. Like, the amount of time he spent dominating the ball was excruciating to watch. And as always, it's the moments he chooses to think it's his time that do my head in: Bucks down eight with 50 seconds to go, he tries to go it alone, and gets stripped. Don't even get me started on the free throw shooting; like, good job getting there that many times, but man, how an established NBA wing can shoot that poorly from the stripe is beyond me. Had nothing for Franz Wagner as his primary defender.

31 minutes, 14 points, 11 rebounds, 3 assists, 2 steals, 4 turnovers, 5 PF, 5/9 FG, 4/7 3P, -3

I'm trying not to reduce my analysis to "Turner made shots, so he played well," even though there is a lot of truth to that. I did think the big man competed more on the interior than in previous games, and he pulled down some highly contested defensive rebounds because of that. Also, Turner's tap-outs on the offensive glass were great; he had four O-boards, and I reckon most, if not all, would've come via tap-outs. Too many turnovers, though.

17 minutes, 10 points, 6 rebounds, 1 assist, 1 steal, 1 block, 4/6 FG, 2/3 3P, -5

Steady progression for Ware, who was solid yet again. The three-ball finally dropped, and he was engaged on defence. I really liked his positioning and ability to play two in the drop, especially on Franz Wagner, whom he deterred from shooting at least a few times while also not giving up the lob.

19 minutes, 3 points, 4 rebounds, 3 assists, 1/4 FG, 1/2 3P, -4

Burries made a nice pull-up three, but is really struggling to find ways to score. Granted, Burries' role is a bit harder than Ament's because they are asking him to be a creator, while Ament is playing more as a converter.

22 minutes, 9 points, 3 rebounds, 1 assist, 2 steals, 0 turnovers, 3/8 FG, 2/5 3P, -1

Setting the shooting stats aside, most of the shots Ament took in his 1/6 first half were good shots, coming off dribble penetration or driving the closeout. The one iffy shot was the dribble-up three off no passes. Then in the second half, those same shots began to fall. Ament was mostly a help defender against the Magic, and while I thought he was largely fine, he did have a few more moments where he spaced out off the ball; namely, an important possession late where he overhelped on the driver, leaving Trisatn da Silva in the corner, who pumped and drove to the rim for the easy jam.

16 minutes, 1 point, 0/4 FG, 0/2 3P, 1/3 FT, -8

Trent took the right shots, but none of them dropped. He really has no chance on defence, but we already knew that.

Jenkins certainly raised some eyebrows by starting Dieng, playing him for five minutes, and then never putting him back on. Not sure what the point of that was, but I do want to note that I was looking for Dieng's bright orange shoes on the bench and couldn't see them, so maybe he was sick or something? The Bucks didn't put anything out, as far as I can tell, so I have to assume he was available. I also didn't entirely understand the Trent minutes, assuming that was, in fact, a basketball decision. Otherwise, I found the constant Kuzma usage down the stretch nauseating, but how much of the blame for that should go to Jenkins? I'm not sure. As for Jenkins' game plan for Orlando's offence, Milwaukee restricted them to 107 points, which, given the Bucks' recent defensive struggles, is a great outcome (though the Magic definitely missed a fair few open shots).

DNP-CD: Caris LeVert, Bogoljub Markovic, Kasparas Jakucionis, Jericho Sims

Inactive: Kam Jones, Cormac Ryan, Pete Nance

The Bucks need to spend entire practice sessions shooting free throws. Kuzma can stay until sundown.

Jenkins on Ryan Rollins: "I thought Ryan was great. He was disruptive. I ended up playing him a super long stretch there in the second half just because of his impact. He was rebounding the ball well and impacting drives… I thought he was making winning plays."

Jenkins on Franz Wagner: "He's a stud of a player. He can finish at the rim, hit floaters. He was hitting threes tonight, finding his teammates. We just didn't execute our coverages on him, and he made us pay. Heck of a player."

The Bucks got smashed in paint points (44-26); I'd bet a lot of those came on lobs. Major disparity in fast break points too (19-4). On the other hand, Milwaukee's bench destroyed Orlando's (50-22).

The Bucks got six three-pointers from their centres.

The Bucks are back in action at home on Sunday night against the Atlanta Hawks. Catch the game at 7:00 p.m. CST on MY24.

#2621. Steelers activate DT Derrick Harmon off injured reserve

One of Pittsburgh's best run defenders is back to help bolster an already successful defensive line.

The Steelers announced on Saturday afternoon that defensive tackle Derrick Harmon has been activated off injured reserve. Cornerback Terrell Smith was waived to create room on the 53-man roster.

Harmon is still listed as questionable ahead of the Steelers' Week 10 matchup, but his activation is a good sign for his availability.

Harmon suffered a foot injury in the first half of the Steelers' loss at Cleveland on Thursday, Oct. 1. He was placed on IR and missed the next five weeks (four games).

His last full game was against the Bengals on Sept. 27. In four games, Harmon logged 12 tackles, one tackle for loss, one forced fumble, and one sack.

The 2025 first-round pick is a significant component of Pittsburgh's run defense, a unit that gave up an average of over 80 yards more on the ground last year (five games) when Harmon was out of the lineup.

This season, regardless of whether Harmon has played, the Steelers are a top-five unit. Patrick Graham's defense is allowing 83.9 rushing yards per game, third in the NFL. The Steelers only allowed 100 yards once in his absence.

Harmon returns for arguably the biggest game in the AFC this season as the Steelers face the Bengals on Sunday Night Football. The winner will hold sole possession of first place in the AFC North and the Steelers would own a two-game lead in Cincinnati after sweeping the season series against their rival.

#2620. Jakobe Thomas gave Kirk Cousins No. 8 for nothing (other than wins)

The Raiders arguably could have driven a harder bargain over the trade that sent quarterback Kirk Cousins back to the Vikings. Vikings safety Jakobe Thomas could have driven a harder bargain over the return of Cousins’s preferred number.

#2617. Bengals could end up with more egg on their face from Arnold Ebiketie trade debacle

The NFL's system to decide who gets compensatory draft picks is complicated, and that's an understatement.

As it stands right now, the Cincinnati Bengals will receive an extra third-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft due to the free agency loss of Trey Hendrickson to the Ravens. And that's one of the reasons the Bengals ended up backing out of their trade with the Eagles for edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie on Tuesday before the deadline came at 4 PM.

The Bengals, a little before noon, agreed to send a sixth-round pick to the Eagles in exchange for Ebiketie, but after OverTheCap.com's Nick Korte pointed that the Bengals could lose their compensatory pick in the trade went through, the Bengals backed out.

A press conference in which the head coach apologized on behalf of the de facto GM later, and the entire team had a decent amount of egg on their face.

The Seattle Seahawks signed former Bengals guard Cordell Volson to their practice squad. If he were to make the active roster and play enough snaps as a starter for the Seahawks, he could, potentially, count as a compensatory free agent, which could give the Bengals an extra seventh-round pick and have allowed that Ebiketie trade to go through without sacrificing the third-round compensatory pick.

Again, this is a big "what if" scenario, and I can't even pretend I know the ins and outs of the compensatory system (there are few that do… especially inside the offices of Paycor Stadium), but wouldn't it just seem to work out that way for the Bengals?

#2616. Dak Prescott Has Different Way of Seeing Cowboys-49ers Game

The Dallas Cowboys have an important and tough matchup coming up for them, as Dak Prescott and company are scheduled to host the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday at AT&T Stadium in Arlington.

The Cowboys have not had much luck in their most recent meetings with the NFC West's 49ers. In fact, Dallas has gone winless in their last four matchups against San Francisco.

That being said, it's not influencing the way Prescott is looking at the game.

"I want to beat them absolutely," Prescott said, via Jon Machota of The Athletic. "And I'm not naive to what has happened or my history against them. But to put that on the rest of these guys or put that on the locker room, I think that's stupid."

Oct 18, 2026; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Dallas Cowboys Dak Prescott (4) passes the football against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Ross Harried-Imagn Images

Instead, the former Mississippi State Bulldogs star quarterback is approaching the 49ers game from a different and seemingly less vengeful and more professional perspective.

"This is about us going in and getting a win. And us trying to win this game and get some momentum going and get back-to-back wins for the first time this season and build off of that. So, what a great opportunity to get to do it against a 7-1 team. It just so happens that it be the Niners."

Prescott acknowledges San Francisco's strength, but has belief in the Cowboys' ability to pull off a stunner in front of their home fans.

"Obviously I want to get a win and everybody in this building does for a bunch of different reasons, added the four-time Pro Bowler. "But at the end of the day, it's a 7-1 team coming in here and we've got an opportunity to beat them. We've got to go do everything we can to get that done."

The Niners game is important for Dallas, which is still trying to catch the New York Giants atop the division standings. With the Giants losing Thursday to the Washington Commanders, the Cowboys have a chance to further narrow the gap to the top spot in the NFC East.

#2614. NFL news, live updates: Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker III out for Week 10, per reports

The 2026 NFL trade deadline is officially in the rearview mirror, and we're on to Week 10, where we'll see a couple of players in new uniforms this week — and some in their old uniforms.

Kirk Cousins rejoined the Minnesota Vikings this week via a trade with the Las Vegas Raiders. He will officially don purple this weekend against the Green Bay Packers after head coach Kevin O'Connell officially named him the team's Week 10 starter on Friday. He'll make his return to Minnesota against the very team he last faced as a Viking, when he suffered a season-ending Achilles tear. He'll look to give the offense a much-needed boost to complement Brian Flores' defense after the team's 6-2 start.

With the trade of Cousins, the Raiders officially named 2026 No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza as their starter moving forward. He'll face a tough schedule to kick off his career as a starting quarterback, with the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos on deck in Weeks 10 and 11.

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates and more ahead of Week 10.

After a great deal of speculation was made that Jonathan Taylor could be moved ahead of the NFL trade deadline, the Indianapolis Colts are reportedly standing pat.

The team will not trade him ahead of the deadline, NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported Tuesday afternoon.

Pelissero reported that the Colts had received multiple offers for Taylor of a second-round pick-plus, but instead, the team will move forward with him as a foundational piece within the locker room as they look to rebuild.

The Patriots added backup running back TreVeyon Henderson to injured reserve on Saturday.

This will sideline him for at least four games. Henderson has been sidelined due to an unexplained medical emergency that involved neurological symptoms. Exact details of what happened to Henderson are not available, but in a statement he released, Henderson said that things are positive.

The New England running back will be first eligible to return in Week 15 ahead of the Patriots' "Monday Night Football" game against the Kansas City Chiefs.

The Carolina Panthers announced Saturday that they've activated wide receiver Xavier Legette from injured reserve.

Legette, a 2024 first-round pick, has been sidelined by a knee injury, which he suffered in a Week 2 win over the Atlanta Falcons.

He could be available for the Panthers' latest divisional matchup, a Sunday road showdown versus the New Orleans Saints.

Legette is still listed as "questionable" on the team's injury report.

Montgomery practiced on Thursday and Friday, but will miss another game after being out since Week 5. Woody Marks, who has compiled 192 rushing yards on 52 attempts, will again be RB1.

Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III will not play in Week 10 after suffering a groin injury in practice this week, NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported Saturday.

Walker leads the NFL with 109 rushing yards per game and is averaging a career-high 5.5 yards per carry. He has seen a heavy workload this season, just 69 carries short of his previous career high for a season, despite being just eight games into the season.

Etienne has been on injured reserve since Week 4 after suffering a hamstring injury. The running back is in his first season with the Saints and has 128 yards on 30 rushes this season.

The Saints opened Etienne's 21-day practice window this week. After being limited earlier in the week, he was a full participant on Friday.

New Orleans is set to take on the Panthers in Week 10.

Barry Anderson and Duane Heydt, who normally serve as umpires, along with side judge Don Willard will take on referee duties on Sunday.

Anderson will officiate the Jacksonville Jaguars-Tennessee Titans game in Tennessee;; Heydt has been assigned to work the Carolina Panthers-New Orleans Saints game in New Orleans; and Willard will have double-duty first refereeing the Miami Dolphins-Indianapolis Colts game in Indianapolis at 1 p.m. ET before making the trip to Cincinnati for Sunday night's game between the Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers at 8:20 p.m. ET.

"Each of the league's 17 officiating crews have a backup referee identified, and that individual trains throughout the year to work at the referee position should the need arise," the NFL said.

According to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero, Jacobs should return to action "in the next few weeks."

The Packers running back fractured his right ring finger last week against the Patrios. Green Bay has not announced a timeline for return. For now, Jacobs has not been placed on injured reserve, which would keep him out at least four weeks.

The San Francisco 49ers traded for veteran wideout Keenan Allen this week, but they're getting another reinforcement Sunday on the road against the Dallas Cowboys. Fellow receiver Deebo Samuel Sr., who has missed the past three games while recovering from a hamstring issue, has been cleared to play.

The Niners will, however, still be without Mike Evans. His Achilles injury will keep him out for a third straight game.

As expected, the Minnesota Vikings have named Kirk Cousins their starting quarterback for Week 10's matchup against the Green Bay Packers. That will mark his first start with the organization since 2023, when his season ended prematurely after tearing his Achilles (coincidentally, against the Packers at Lambeau).

It remains unclear who will back up Cousins in Week 10. Kyler Murray has been dealing with a hamstring injury, and Carson Wentz … well, he solidified the team's need to trade for Cousins in the first place with a disastrous start against the Buffalo Bills on "Monday Night Football."

New Orleans Saints running back Travis Etienne Jr. was a full participant in Friday's practice, though he's still listed as questionable on the team's injury report with a hamstring issue.

Asked if he'll play on Sunday versus the Carolina Panthers, Etienne said, "I hope so. I definitely want to."

Etienne hasn't played since Week 3, when he rushed for 57 yards on 13 carries in a 35-27 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders. His 128 yards currently rank fourth on a Saints team that ranks second-to-last in the NFC (and fifth in the NFL) in rushing offense.

Walker, who is second in the NFL with 872 rushing yards, reported a tight groin on Friday morning and did not take part in Friday's practice. Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said that the running back will get treatment and the team will see how he feels on Saturday.

Pickens did not play during last week's win over the Colts and was limited in practice this week. But judging by his response to being asked if he'd be available in Week 10, the Cowboys wide receiver will be on the field.

Both player could return this week when the Patriots face the Lions in Munich. Brown traveled with the team to Germany and, along with running back Rhamondre Stevenson (knee), has looked "pretty good" in practice this week, according to head coach Mike Vrabel.

Brown has been limited to three games this season and has been out since Week 7. He is listed as questionable for Sunday, along with Stevenson.

On Sunday in Las Vegas, Mendoza will receive his first NFL start. The football gods have not gifted him breaks. The Raiders host the Seattle Seahawks, who have allowed the fewest yards per game in the NFL through nine weeks. Only three defenses across the league have allowed fewer points. Adding to the chess match nuances, as well as the heightened emotions: Kubiak will be scheming against the team whose offense he coordinated to the Super Bowl nine months prior. Play-callers will know each other intimately. Kubiak hopes Mendoza does not feel pressure rests on his shoulders alone.

"We have an awareness of his situation and being in his first game," Kubiak said. "However, we're not peeling back anything and we're going to go do what the whole team does best, all 11. …

"He's got to do his job and not worry about a whole lot else. Everybody does their 1/11th, and everything around him elevates their play."

Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that the wide receiver is on the verge of being available against the Bills on Sunday.

Wilson has been in concussion protocol since getting injured in Week 8. He is expected to practice on Friday and has one more hurdle to clear before getting the green light.

Two Jaguars acquisitions this week, safety Jessie Bates and defensive tackle Jordan Davis, will not play against the Titans. Head coach Liam Coen said that the fact that both players have not had their bye week yet was a factor.

Bates, who came from the Falcons, would have gone on his bye with Atlanta in Week 11. Davis would have been on his bye this week had he not been dealt from the Eagles.

Davon Godchaux, who was also acquired this week, will play after going on his bye in Week 8 while with the Saints.

St. Brown, whose mother is originally from Germany and is fluent in the language, tried to teach his head coach some words with the team playing in Munich this week against the Patriots.

Dan Campbell wanted to know how to say "spread your wings" in German, but to also add "f***" to the phrase. He looked it up himself and somehow manage to use the word for "s***" instead, which led to St. Brown teaching his coach what not say.

Brown, who signed a one-year deal to join the Eagles in March after two seasons with the Chiefs, didn't see much action with Philadelphia. He suited up for four games and made just five receptions on eight targets.

#2613. Dejounte Murray is available: should the Raptors pay the price?

The case of Dejounte Murray is an interesting one. The Raptors' fanbase seems captivated on two things right now, as the team is experiencing a slump with both Kawhi Leonard and Scottie Barnes out: a new centre, and a new point guard. It seems that one way or another, the people want change. But is Dejounte Murray the right player to bring it?

Murray's history speaks for itself. A defensively minded point guard who could score and facilitate, he was a big part of those pre-Alien San Antonio Spurs teams, before ending up on the New Orleans Pelicans in a mire of injury troubles. For the past few years, Murray has had few opportunities to play basketball, at all, and when he's been on the court, he's not been All-Star he once was.

INGLEWOOD, CA – NOVEMBER 8: Dejounte Murray #5 of the New Orleans Pelicans looks on during the game against the LA Clippers on November 8, 2026 at Intuit Dome in Los Angeles, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Juan Ocampo/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images

His contract, for a Raptors team that is currently struggling financially, is a breath of fresh air. Making just over $32 million this season, Murray becomes an unrestricted free-agent at the end of the 2027-28 campaign, meaning that he could either be traded, released, or re-signed for a more team-friendly contract, alleviating the Raptors' financial pressures.

Immanuel Quickley, the Raptors' starter at the one, is making $32.5 million until the 2028-29 season, so it would be easy to make the money, and the position, work for the Raptors. Moving off Quickley could allow for Jamal Shead to firmly step into the starting lineup as a pass-first point guard as opposed to Quickley's place as a floor-spacing combo guard, who perhaps plays more naturally at the two. And, if they were to keep Murray, the Raptors would have the flexibility to make big moves and engender what would perhaps be a more stable situation, while retaining the services of a former All-Star. But, is Murray really an upgrade over IQ?

Many complaints have been made about Quickley, but he is also a bonafide volume shooter, something the Raptors desperately need as a part of their offensive schemes. Murray is many things, but he hasn't taken six or more threes per game since 2024. And while Quick is far from an iron man, he played 70 regular season games last year. Again, Murray hasn't done that since… 2024.

On a team with Kawhi Leonard and Jakob Poeltl, there is no sense in getting a third injury-prone starter on the squad, unless the front office is actively trying to tank. And if Murray ends up injured again for the third season in a row, there's no saying what value he'd bring on the trade market. Betting on one players' health is one thing, and betting on that of two is a stretch. But three is just ludicrous, and if you saw your buddy gambling that magnitude in a casino, you'd haul him out of there.

Beyond the on-court realities, Dejounte Murray is someone who actively disrespected Jamal Shead last season, someone who is an increasingly important part of this Raptors' team. That situation, where Murray dropped Shead and got up in his face after hitting the shot, was ugly as sin. Immanuel Quickley ran up to Murray to stick up for his teammate, and the whole thing just puts a bad taste in my mouth regarding what a trade for the point guard would look like.

Frankly, I'm all for aggressiveness and competitiveness, but considering that Murray and Shead didn't have any sort of known rivalry, this move was just disrespectful. Bringing that energy into the Raps' locker room doesn't seem to be the right move when this team's success seems so heavily predicated on good chemistry.

The reality for the Raptors is that unless their starters' health and production stay unrealistically consistent, they may very well have to make a trade to get this team looking right in the postseason. But, there's no sense in making moves, just for the sake of making moves.

Trying to clear cap space is likely going to be a need, but doing that without a clear plan is not worth it, especially if it results in sacrificing one of Toronto's best options for floor spacing, which its starting lineup already struggles with. Clearly, based on this summer, the front office is willing and able to wait for good deals to come by, and there are very few worlds in which a deal for Dejounte Murray is a good one for Toronto.

#2611. Patriots place TreVeyon Henderson on IR, activate 2 on eve of Lions game

The New England Patriots made a series of transactions on the eve of their Week 10 game against the Detroit Lions, including placing running back TreVeyon Henderson on injured reserve. In addition, interior offensive lineman Greg Van Roten and fullback Reggie Gilliam were both activated from IR.

Furthermore, the Patriots decided to elevate interior offensive lineman Andrew Rupcich from the practice squad to the game day roster for Sunday.

Henderson, 24, has been sidelined since Oct. 29 due to an illness. Earlier this month, he shared an update on his status on social media and explained that he had recently "experienced an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms that required hospitalization for several days."

A second-round draft pick by the Patriots in 2025, the Ohio State product finished his rookie campaign with 1,132 scrimmage yards and 10 touchdowns. His sophomore season, however, was a challenging one even before his recent illness: serving as the Patriots' No. 2 behind Rhamondre Stevenson, Henderson missed time due to two separate ankle injuries sustained in August and October, respectively, and as a consequence was limited to six games as well as 57 touches for 248 scrimmage yards and one touchdown.

With his move to IR freeing up a roster spot, the Patriots were able to activate two players.

Van Roten, 36, arrived in New England during preseason after an then-top backup interior offensive lineman Ben Brown suffered an injury. On his ninth different team since entering the NFL in 2012, he remained on the roster even after Brown's return and was the first man up when right guard Mike Onwenu fractured his ankle in Week 2. Unfortunately for the veteran backup, he himself sustained a thigh injury in his first start the following week and subsequently had to be placed on injured reserve as well.

Gilliam, 29, signed a three-year, $10.8 million free agency contract with the Patriots in March. Taking over the fullback position upon his arrival, he played 58 offensive snaps and 32 on special teams over the first four weeks of the season; he caught one 4-yard pass along the way. Gilliam also sustained a knee injury at one point and in Week 4 against his former team, the Bills, added an ankle issue. That second injury prompted the Patriots to send him to IR a few days later.

Both Van Roten and Gilliam had previously returned to practice to open their 21-day return windows. Van Roten returned last week alongside Mack Hollins, but unlike the wide receiver was not activated ahead of last Sunday's game against the Packers. Van Roten made his return to the practice fields before the Patriots boarded their flight to Germany on Wednesday.

The Patriots furthermore elevated the aforementioned Andrew Rupcich from the practice squad. With Van Roten only now returning, Ben Brown being ruled out of the game with a knee injury, and Walter Rouse questionable after entering concussion protocol this week, he provides experienced emergency depth up front.

The Patriots will take on the Lions at Munich's Allianz Arena at 9:30 a.m. ET on Sunday.

#2610. Alperen Sengun’s 43 points leads Rockets over Jazz 125-118

Sorry for the late recap, y'all. Our writer was stuck in airport mess, and I didn't find out until this morning. Anyway, the Houston Rockets won their thrid game in a row on Friday night after a monster game from Alperen Sengun, defeating the Jazz 125-118. Alpie went for 43 points, 12 rebounds, and 5 assists on 17-for-24 shooting, becoming just the third player in Rockets history alongside Hakeem Olajuwon and Yao Ming to put up that stat line on 70 percent-plus shooting.

The Rockets also got 22 points and 6 assists from Kevin Durant, who showed off some passing chops in this one despite shooting just 5-for-14. They got 17 points, 3 assists and zero turnovers from Fed VanVleet, 12 points and 10 boards for Amen Thompson, as well as 14 points and 11 boards from Tari Eason off of the bench.

This game was closer than it needed to be at home against the 1-11 Jazz, as the Jazz held close into the final minutes until VanVleet closed to door with some timely scoring to thankfully not waste Sengun's nuclear night.

Jabari Smith Jr. and Reed Sheppard combined to go 2-for-16 from the field and 1-for-11 from three, so the Rockets had to get role player help elsewhere — Bogdan Bogdanovich went 3-for-4 from deep for 11 points — and the defense wasn't nearly as tight as it should have been against a bottom-feeder. The Rockets did allow the Jazz to shoot 46 percent, but they ultimately pulled off the win to move to 10-3 on the season.

The Jazz were led by Darryn Peterson with 28 points, Keyonte George with 27 and Ace Bailey with 21.

The Rockets are off tonight, but they will return to action on Sunday, where they will kick off a back-to-back set with a matchup against the Washington Wizards, rolling into another road game against the Miami Heat on Monday.

#2608. NBA Cup 2026 updated standings after Friday's group play games

Friday's Emirates NBA Cup group stage action showcased nine games, with several teams delivering standout performances while others endured close defeats or suffered blowout losses.

The San Antonio Spurs continued their commanding run in the NBA Cup, remaining unbeaten after a dominant 123-85 victory over the Golden State Warriors. The Warriors were without their star, Stephen Curry, who is sidelined for at least two weeks due to a right oblique tear. Stephon Castle stepped up for the Spurs, leading all scorers with a season-high 32 points, while Victor Wembanyama contributed a double-double performance with 12 points and 12 rebounds.

Despite a 40-point performance from two-time MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, the Oklahoma City Thunder could not pull it off in the final moments. Gilgeous-Alexander narrowly missed a 21-foot jumper that could have secured the win against the LA Clippers. Instead, the Clippers captured their first NBA Cup group play victory, surviving a 113-112 thriller and handing the Thunder their third consecutive loss.

The Indiana Pacers secured their first NBA Cup win in dramatic fashion, edging out the defending champions, the New York Knicks, in a 106-104 contest. Pascal Siakam led the Pacers with 19 points, while Aaron Nesmith added 18 points to seal their victory and improve their record to 1-1 in group play.

#2607. Mike Matthews injury updates: Latest on leading Tennessee receiver after hurting knee

As Tennessee continues its push for an SEC championship game berth and a spot in the College Football Playoff, it may have to do so without one of its best offensive players.

Vols wide receiver Mike Matthews left the team's Week 11 game at Texas A&M in the second quarter with an injury on Saturday, Nov. 14.

The injury occurred after Matthews brought in a 17-yard pass to get Tennessee a first down at the Texas A&M 11-yard line. Matthews was brought down to the turf awkwardly by a group of Aggies defenders as he was fighting for extra yardage. After the play was over, Matthews remained on the turf in visible pain and took his helmet off.

More: Wake Forest is wrecking teams. Could it help ACC steal second CFP bid?

He was helped off of the field by trainers and taken into the injury tent on the Vols' sideline at Kyle Field in College Station, Texas.

Matthews is Tennessee's leading receiver this season, with 37 catches for 566 yards and four touchdowns heading into Saturday's game.

As Matthews was being helped off the field, he was unable to put any weight on his right leg, offering some insight into the kind of pain he was enduring.

According to ESPN sideline reporter Taylor McGregor, Matthews was "very emotional" as he came to the sideline and "you could tell he was in a lot of pain."

ESPN's broadcast crew later noted that it was a knee injury.

After going into the injury tent, Matthews reemerged with crutches and appeared to be heading back to the Tennessee locker room, but the severity of his injury has not yet been determined.

Before exiting the game, Matthews had two catches for 42 yards. The reception on which he was injured helped set up a 30-yard field goal to get the No. 9 Vols within one, 7-6. Tennessee enters the game with a 7-2 record and a 4-2 mark in the SEC, which helped it get to No. 8 in the latest playoff selection committee rankings.

"Mike was playing really well," Tennessee coach Josh Heupel said during his halftime interview with ESPN. "The next guy's got to step up."

Despite that success, the Vols have dealt with nine season-ending injuries to players this season: running back Daune Morris (broken leg); starting defensive end Tyree Weathersby (knee); starting left guard Wendell Moe; starting safety Edrees Farooq (knee); starting tight end Ethan Davis (knee); safety Dylan Lewis (foot); wide receiver/kick returner Joakim Dodson (leg); linebacker Jaedon Harmon (knee); and cornerback Jadais Richard (upper-body).

#2606. Knicks Bulletin: ‘I tweaked my calf’

Fake comeback attempt by New York on Friday.

Fake concerning development across the nation's airspace, too.

Here's a bunch of the latest, including some interesting Josh Hart revelations.

On the decision to draw up the final shot for Karl-Anthony Towns instead of Jalen Brunson:

"We needed a 2-pointer. We had executed something like that in practice. We thought we would gain an advantage with a little rip screen. KAT got a great look. Probably a shot that he makes nine out of 10 times. So I'm okay with it."

On what really led to the Knicks' loss to Indiana:

"That play was something we liked, and we went to it. But I'll say this: That play did not cost us the game. We were lucky a little bit, and our guys did fight to give us a chance down the stretch. But I don't care who you play, it's going to be hard to win a game on the road when you lose the possession game like we did, if we get blown by on defense as bad as we did, if you let your opponent win the physicality battle like we did. It's all a recipe for a loss. And that's where I'm disappointed."

"I don't know if we fouled that much, but we were fouling. They just could keep putting their head down and driving into us, and we weren't ready to play. We didn't do our work early and get in the stance, being ready to guard these guys off the dribble drive, and they just walked to the free-throw line time after time after time."

On his reaction to the no-call on OG Anunoby's drive to the basket:

"I did get a T, but the reality of it is they were playing harder than us. It was out of frustration. Some of it because we just had a game that we played, and you have a guy like Jalen [Brunson] who's an All-Star and an MVP candidate; he goes 0-0 from the free-throw line. And at the end of the first half [here], I think it was maybe 20 to three or something like that, and that in itself is frustrating.

"To know that we're getting beat that bad from the free-throw line, and they're missing some calls. Now, are we fouling? Yes, and we got to do a better job doing our work earlier. But in the same breath, the discrepancy shouldn't be that bad two games in a row. Hopefully not three games in a row coming up.

"And that's what I'm taking a look at. That there are some fouls that they're calling with our body because guys are just putting their head down and running into you and snapping their head back, but we're not getting those same calls, and that is the frustrating part."

On the Knicks' inconsistent offensive rhythm and the need to improve:

"No, not yet. Not yet. At times, yes, but we're not always in a good flow right now, which is fine, because there are other ways to win a basketball game while we're trying to work on that."

On missing the potential game-tying shot against Indiana:

"I thought it was a great shot. I was excited for the opportunity. I got to make a quick decision. It's either OG is open on the rip screen and he has an open layup or I get to take the shot. I just was ready for the opportunity. … I'm happy with the follow through. I was happy with the technique. It just wasn't my day."

On taking full responsibility for his struggles and needing to improve:

"I just look in the mirror, I just got to be better. Nobody else to blame but me and I just got to go out there and, whatever it is, just be better and go harder.

"When times are tough, you just gotta own up to it and just be better.

"I try to be my best throughout the whole year. Obviously, struggles come, which obviously nobody wants, but like I said, in these moments, gotta look in the mirror and you're tested the most and just see what you're made of. So, just gotta be better.

On the Knicks' crowded wing rotation and the possibility of roster changes:

"There are several different ways you can look at it. You can look at it, if [Shamet and McBride] have it going, cool. Good. You could look at it like, 'Okay, maybe something else has to change [like a trade].'

"But there's going to good days with that, bad days. But whatever allows the Knicks the best opportunity and chance to win, that's the most important."

On the Knicks' slow pace limiting the effectiveness of Mikal Bridges and OG Anunoby:

"There's less chances at the rim. I think it also affects Mikal and OG. … [Coach Mike Brown] says Mikal is the best runner in the league. So if you have the best runner in the league and you're not running, you're wasting one of his talents. If we play faster, we'll be able to do that. Sometimes OG has smaller guards defending him, so if we run he can be able to seal at the rim, be able to get easy points at the rim, which also can help our rim finishing."

On speeding up the Knicks' offense even if Jalen Brunson doesn't bring the ball up the court:

"We gotta get the ball out and sometimes that might have to be [Brunson] just running and not going to the ball after a make or a defensive rebound. Just trying to get a better and quicker flow so it's not so stagnant in the halfcourt."

On how his calf and ankle injuries disrupted his conditioning and preparation for the season:

"This year was a little different. Obviously, a shorter break in terms of the summer [because of the long playoff run] but also I wasn't physically able to really push my body towards the end of the summer to be prepared for the season. I had [the calf] injury in September, which kept me out for about three weeks, so I wasn't able to get in some of that conditioning and some of those legs under me, which is normally the time to do it.

"And then, the ankle injury in training camp. So, the ramp up was a little bit slower than I kinda wanted it to be or kinda liked it to be, so I think that's the biggest thing is just getting my legs under me."

On his shooting struggles and the impact of missing several weeks of basketball activity:

"The shots I'm shooting, I like them. I think that was kinda evident with Cleveland. One of the things: All three of my 3s was just hella short. It was just, those legs, get those legs under me.

"Also, on top of that, missing a week in the season, it's cumulative of six, seven weeks of just not much activity basketball-wise. So, I think that's just what it is. So, as the season progresses and I'm out there running more, doing all those kinds of things, the performance will follow."

On his mental struggles following the loss to Indiana:

"Just have to be better. Have to be better mentally. I just gotta get my mental right."

On not knowing how to improve his mental state and on-court performance:

"Wish I could tell you. Don't know. … I gotta figure out how to improve that and improve my play."

On why he has struggled to finish shots around the rim:

"It's early. We're not where we wanna be, but it's November. Everything needs to be better."

On the need for staying ready and responding to adversity:

"You're playing well one day and [then] next time you get punched in the mouth. So it's always about how you respond in this league."

#2602. The Fernando Mendoza era marks a sizeable shift for rebuilding Raiders

By trading former starter Kirk Cousins for a third-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, the Las Vegas Raiders are turning to the top pick in the 2026 draft Fernando Mendoza at quarterback. The move from a 38-year-old veteran to the 23-year-old rookie marks a sizeable shift for the Silver & Black.

"Our expectation is for him to lead the offense, to lead the operation, and to go play a game here Sunday and be the leader of the team, be the leader of the offense," Las Vegas head coach Klint Kubiak said of Mendoza. "We have to prepare him and give him a lot of reps to get him comfortable. So, our expectation is for him to lead the offense."

Standing 6-foot-5 and 225 pounds, Mendoza brings NFL-size with a livelier arm and fresh legs with mobility to the quarterback position, as opposed to Cousins. But where the veteran has the rook beat is game experience. While Cousins may be a statue as a pocket passer, he did provide his younger counterpart an ideal mentor and sounding board. And Las Vegas is banking on the nine games Mendoza sat and watched Cousins operate provided a blueprint for the rookie to follow.

And what an opponent for Mendoza to make his first start against: The Seattle Seahawks.

"Like I said, this is a new experience. It's great. It's against a fantastic opponent. However, I have so much trust in the coaching staff, in the front office, and my teammates and the leaders of the team to go out there and best support everybody's 1/11th, so we can do our job to the best ability."

While Seattle is quite shaky offensively — ranking 18th in points scored and 17th in yards gained under rookie offensive coordinator Brian Fleury — head coach and defensive play caller Mike Macdonald has the Seahawks defense as one of the top units in the NFL.

If both Mendoza and Kubiak are to get the Raiders aerial attack on track this Sunday, they'll have to do it against the Seahawks' top-ranked passing defense which is ranked No. 1 in air yards allowed (1,396). Seattle is also allowing the fourth-least passing touchdowns (nine) and have racked up the sixth-most interceptions (eight).

Both the Raiders quarterback and head coach are eager to meet the challenge head-on, though.

"It is, yeah. And every week in the NFL is tough, and this is the best defense in the NFL," Kubiak said when asked about Mendoza's start against a top-tier Seahawks defense being invaluable. "And again, he's got to go do his job and not worry about a whole lot else. Everybody does their 1/11th, and everyone around him elevates their play."

Notice that 1/11th that both Mendoza and Kubiak were quick to drop during their respective times at the podium during media availability this week leading up the Week 10 matchup with the Seahawks?

Kubiak's offense epitomizes the all-11 approach. Ranked eighth in the NFL in points scored (238) and 15th in yards gained (2,979), Las Vegas passing game is ranked fifth in air yards (2,337) and are third-best in touchdowns (20). The offensive line — which has showcased much better pass protection ability than run blocking — kept Cousins upright for those 20 touchdowns and the expectation is the group doing the same for Mendoza.

The stronger arm talent the Indiana product brings to the table should pay dividends for Raiders pass catchers like tight end Brock Bowers (team-leading 48 receptions, 658 yards, and six touchdowns), fleet-footed wide receiver Tre Tucker (33 receptions for 529 yards and four touchdowns), and running back Ashton Jeanty (42 receptions for 371 yards and three touchdowns. Add tight end Michael Mayer (39 catches for 388 yards and a touchdown), and Mendoza has weaponary at his disposal.

Las Vegas' ground game is in the pits, however, and is ranked dead-last in yards gained (642) and yards per carry average (2.9). Much of this is due to lack of trench dominance and opposing defenses loading the box with eight defenders knowing Cousins presents zero threat to scramble and take off with his legs. Perhaps the Mendoza dynamic changes that for Kubiak's offense?

"But, hey, go through your progression, and obviously if it's not there, you've got to go run the football. And then when you're running the football, how do you protect yourself so that you can get us to the next down, because we need you available for the whole season," Kubiak said regarding Mendoza trusting his eyes, staying in the pocket, and run as a last resort rather than too quickly. "You're not trying to sell out for a yard on first-and-10, so it's an ongoing learning process. But that's also why when you're selecting men in the draft, you identify their instincts. I liked Fernando's instincts in college, and it's his first NFL game. So, we're all going to see. But I'm excited for his opportunity and just for the whole offense to go play together."

We're going to find out if Kubiak's quarterback-whisperer ways can transfer to Mendoza as it has with Sam Darnold (during the Raiders head coach's time as Seattle offensive coordinator last season) and Cousins.

While this game features the debut of Mendoza and matching up against Macdonald's defense, underneath all this is this simple item between the Raiders and Seahawks: Kubiak misses Macdonald's defense (Las Vegas' group is led by rookie defensive coordinator Rob Leonard and ranks dead last in points allowed (268) and yards yielded (3,469)) and Macdonald misses Kubiak's offense.

"Kirk has taught me a multitude of lessons, but two of the ones that stick out right now from your question is, number one, always being prepared and doing everything possible you can to prepare yourself to best serve your teammates, to best serve the organization. So you go out there Sunday, regardless of the result, no doubt in your mind that you did everything possible to give your team and teammates the best chance to perform and win. And second is to be yourself. He's always told everybody on the team, and he was a great leader and captain on the team and really brought us together and had a lot of togetherness. So that's something that I look to exemplify and take from his lessons."

—Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza on what lessons from former starter Kirk Cousins sticks out

#2600. Hawks unable to outlast Bulls in overtime loss

The Atlanta Hawks were in action in the NBA Cup on Friday night but came up short in a 125-117 road loss in overtime against the Chicago Bulls. Jalen Johnson registered a triple-double of 27 points, 11 rebounds, and 10 assists and CJ McCollum added 20 points off the bench. For the Bulls — without star rookie Caleb Wilson — Norman Powell led the way with 33 points with seven Bulls scoring in double-digits.

The Hawks would have entered this game as favorites, with the Bulls heading into this game on the back of an eight-game losing streak and looking for just their second win of the season. Without impressive rookie Caleb Wilson, the Bulls were missing talent that is sorely needed and handed the Hawks a significant advantage with his absence. In reality, that is not how it played out.

The Hawks' time spent leading this game was extremely brief, and it was the Bulls who ran out to a double-digit lead in the first quarter behind 10 first quarter points from Powell. The key difference in this game began to become clear from the first quarter as the Hawks shot 2-of-8 from three-point range as the visitors' struggles shooting the ball became more concrete in the second quarter. The Bulls, meanwhile, had no problem dispatching their three-pointers and began to run their lead to a game-high 18 points in the second quarter.

While the Hawks found some success in the paint — and this was how they began to reign in the Chicago lead — the three-point shooting story was becoming clear: 3-of-17 for Atlanta, while the Bulls shot 11-of-28 from three in the first half. The Hawks were, at times, settling for transition, pull-up threes from above the break but only shot 1-of-11 from such shots in this game:

Off of a miss, Nickeil Alexander-Walker pushes the ball up the floor and springs into a three-pointer, but cannot convert:

Off of the pass from Dyson Daniels, Johnson pulls up into a three-pointer which is missed:

On this attempt, the Hawks work themselves into a better opportunity from above the break, with Alexander-Walker finding Daniels, who finds Onyeka Okongwu all alone above the break, but the three is missed:

The Hawks would continue to strike out on these opportunities all night long, and relied on the inside scoring of Johnson, and some tough, crafty baskets from McCollum to keep the visitors in range, even tying the game in late stages of the third quarter.

The Bulls, however, quickly stretched their lead back to 10 in the fourth quarter, giving the Hawks a lot of work to do on the road. Even with 2:22 remaining the Hawks faced an uphill battle of seven points, but Okongwu and Johnson, tied the game.

Having not led the game since the first quarter — when the game was 7-6 — the Hawks had multiple opportunities to take a late lead in this game. The first comes in the form of the Hawks failing to secure a rebound off of a missed shot from Jalen Smith, with Johnson losing the rebound and the Bulls get the opportunity to call a timeout:

After a missed shot from Powell inside, the Hawks get a chance to get out in transition. Johnson is faced by Josh Giddey, and elects to pass the ball back out to the perimeter to Alexander-Walker, who is unable to hit the three-pointer:

I'm not sure Johnson realized how strong his advantage was here: no help was coming, Giddey was on his own, and it's a one-on-one near the rim you would heavily back Johnson to score or draw a foul. Instead, he makes the unselfish play and finds Alexander-Walker, who continued his unfortunate shooting trend in this game at the wrong time.

The Hawks would get another chance as they advance the ball off of a timeout after another Bulls miss. Okongwu delivers a good pass to the cutting Aaron Wiggins, who is surely rim-side and through for a layup, but cannot complete the catch as the ball slips through his fingers and out of play:

Three differing chances for the Hawks to get/to score and all of them passed them by, and the game goes to overtime.

The Hawks would take their first lead since the first quarter, but it would not last, as Powell scored nine points in the overtime period to pull away from the Hawks before a dagger three Matas Buzelis dashes any hopes of a Hawks victory.

Postgame, Hawks head coach Quin Snyder highlighted the start of the game as an issue for the Hawks and discussed how the Hawks' shooting issues were exacerbated by the Bulls' own good three-point shooting night.

"We didn't play with the force at the beginning of the game," said Snyder postgame. "That impacts our defense, it's, kind of, the complimentary of basketball: how your defense affects your offense. When we're not forceful defensively, or active, and we're not running. We know the things we need to have in the front of our minds to focus on. When we don't do that, we don't play well. By the same token, we started to find that, 18 (points) down. When you're not shooting the ball well — we had a bad shooting night, which is going to happen — those things become even more important. When your opponent is shooting the ball, it compounds itself. We take from it what we can, and there's a lot here we can focus on."

"We've got to come out with energy from the jump, we just didn't do that," added Jalen Johnson.

This game can be summed up by living by the three and dying by the three. The Hawks finished with 8-of-40 from three (20%) while the Bulls shot 20-of-50 from three (40%), and while there are other nuances of this game that did not go the Hawks' way (which we'll touch on in a moment), the game can really be summed up as simply as that. If you hit eight threes while your opponent hits 20 (a 60-24 point disparity) it's difficult to win games consistently. The fact the Hawks almost did, speaks to the nature of the Bulls' season (allowing Jalen Smith to 15 shots and 1-of-6 from three is something the Bulls allowed to happen, for some reason).

From the Hawks' side, it was another difficult night shooting the three from Alexander-Walker, who shot 1-of-11 from three, and 6-of-19 from the field — it just wasn't his night, and there's been a couple of those this season where it becomes evident it may not be his night from three and he ends up with a poor percentage on a high volume. It was the same story across the board: reliable three-point shooters for the Hawks couldn't get their shots to fall. Okongwu shot 2-of-7 from three, while Aaron Wiggins shot 1-of-6 from distance.

Turnovers were also a key feature in this game, with the Hawks committing 17 in total, off of which the Bulls scored 20 points. These turnovers, as Snyder often references along with getting stops, impact the Hawks' ability to establish their identity: it's key for Atlanta to get out on the run in transition/off of a miss and when the Hawks are committing turnovers this impacts the Hawks significantly.

"It's hard to stop the ball when you turn the ball over," said CJ McCollum postgame.

Chicago turnovers were also how the Hawks remained in this game, scoring 34 points off of the Bulls' 24 turnovers — without these, the Hawks would not have been able to close the margin as they did, with Johnson and McCollum credited for 10 points apiece off of Chicago turnovers.

In addition, when the Hawks are off form from three, they are at least able to rack up points in the paint — many of which came off of turnovers — scoring 66 points in the paint, with Johnson accounting for 20 of these. Johnson finished with 27 points on 11-of-26 shooting from the field to go with his triple-double.

The Hawks were chasing the game for much of the affair, but Snyder didn't believe that this pursuit tired the Hawks physically.

"I didn't feel like we were tired," said Snyder. "Powell hit some tough shots in the overtime which I thought we defended pretty well. We made a couple of adjustments that our guys executed that I thought were really good. You put yourself in a position where you've got to make a lot of plays. We made enough to go to get where we were, but the game goes back and forth, and it went back one too many times."

There's no doubt the Hawks left themselves with a lot of work to do, both in the first half and in the fourth quarter when they trailed by double-digits. But they had their chances in regulation, and it slipped through their fingers (well, quite literally in Wiggins' case). In overtime, the quality of Powell (33 points on 12-of-29 shooting) shone through as he seized the game, with enough support from the rest to see the Bulls through.

It's a poor loss for the Hawks, who would have won this game had they hit any number of their 26 missed threes in regulation. They were also off since Monday, while the Bulls were in action on Wednesday, so their flat start to the game looks worse with context. In the context of the NBA Cup, the Hawks still have a positive point differential and are still in play to advance but cannot afford another loss such as this.

The Hawks (7-6) are back in action on Sunday when they will encounter another team on the road desperate for victory: the 1-12 Milwaukee Bucks.

#2599. Connecticut cross country runners shine as Lauren Parrett and Tycen LaBelle take third at New Englands

When talking about what Connecticut runners did at the New England Interscholastic Cross Country Championships on Saturday in Belfast, Maine, one could quote the Talking Heads song "Once in a Lifetime."

Same as it ever was. Same as it ever was.

That's because Glastonbury's Lauren Parrett and Griswold's Tycen LaBelle once again finished third in their respective races. Glastonbury finished fifth as a team, just like they did last year. The girls' race winner, Madeleine Lane of Hopkinton, N.H., was even the same as last year.

#2598. Recap: Miami beats Duke 36-25

The Miami Hurricanes started off their home stretch of ACC games on the right foot, defeating former Canes head coach Manny Diaz and his Duke Blue Devils 36-25 on Saturday afternoon at Hard Rock Stadium.

Former Duke QB Darian Mensah continued his Heisman Trophy campaign going 30/41 for 386 yards with a touchdown and no picks. Javian Mallory was an absolute dude, with 150 scrimmage yards and three touchdowns. Cooper Barkate had a huge day with eight catches for 134 yards. Mo Toure had a team-high 11 combined tackles.

Miami and Duke started off slowly on the offensive side of the ball, with the teams trading off five punts between them in the first quarter. Miami opened the scoring with a 39-yard Jake Weinberg field goal early in the second quarter. Duke answered with a field goal 13 plays later. Miami finally found the end zone on a four-yard run by Mark Fletcher, Jr. who left the game with an apparent injury in the first half and did not return. A 40-yard Barkate catch and run was the big play of the drive.

Duke answered on the following drive, and it was the uber-talented Nate Sheppard who broke free for a 47-yard touchdown right up the middle. Sheppard had a field day with 224 scrimmage yards and two scores. Miami would answer with a chip shot field goal shortly before the half for a 13-10 lead at the break.

The Canes got the ball first and drove down the field thanks to a 33-yard run by Jordan Lyle. And it looked like for a second Elija Lofton finally had his nifty end zone catch he was denied last week. But his one-handed grab was made just after he touched out of bounds and was reversed after review and a field goal followed.

Miami forced a punt near midfield, and minutes later, Mallory took a short pass and went 63 yards weaving through traffic and to the end zone for a touchdown and a 22-10 lead. The blocking was nifty on the play from the backfield down the field. And Shannon Dawson made a truly head-scratching call on the two-point conversion attempt with a designed run to Mensah. Mensah was clobbered just before the goal line and bent backwards. You simply can't risk your QB like that.

Duke would answer back five plays later, with Sheppard cutting left and past Miami's defense and getting to the corner on a five-yard run before throwing the U down over his knee (not sure why people do this).

Miami raised that U right back up on the following drive, which was a death march of over seven and a half minutes that took 17 plays and went 79 yards. Mallory tore through the line and across the goal line from two yards for a two-yard score. Three plays later, Xavier Lucas turned for the ball on a poorly thrown pass by Walker Eget, and the Canes secured their only takeaway of the game. Five plays later, Mallory broke free off the left side for a 39-yard touchdown, and church was officially out at 36-17. Duke would add some window dressing with a last second touchdown throw on fourth down with under 30 seconds left to close out the scoring.

A win, and Miami can clinch a spot in the ACC title game if UNC can knock off Louisvile this evening.

#2597. Alexander Ovechkin announces this will be his last NHL season: 'Let's have fun'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Alex Ovechkin's 22nd NHL season will be his last, the Washington Capitals superstar announced on Monday."This is gonna be my last year," Ovechkin told his teammates in a video the Capitals posted to social media. "It's sad, but it is what it is. We have an unbelievable team this year. There are 82 games left. Let's make the playoffs, and let's have fun."

Ovechkin has already established himself as the greatest goal-scorer in hockey history with 929 tallies, and he still has 82 games to add to that total before he hangs up his skates.

The No. 1 overall pick in the 2004 NHL Draft, Ovechkin immediately established himself as a prolific scorer by notching 52 goals en route to winning the Calder Trophy as a rookie.

Since then, Ovechkin has won the Rocket Richard Trophy as the NHL's leading goal-scorer a record nine times. The Capitals legend's resume also features an Art Ross Trophy and three Hart Trophy wins.

The crowning achievement in Ovechkin's illustrious career is leading Washington to its first Stanley Cup in 2017-18. After coming up short in a number of postseasons prior to that, Ovechkin led all playoff performers with 15 goals and won the Conn Smythe Trophy as a result.

Following the 2025-26 season, there was speculation that Ovechkin could retire, but he signed an incentive-laden one-year deal with the Caps.Sensing that this could be Ovechkin's final season, the Capitals loaded up to give their franchise icon one more shot at the Stanley Cup. Washington signed former Buffalo Sabres winger Alex Tuch in free agency and acquired winger Jordan Kyrou from the St. Louis Blues via trade.

No team is as loaded on the wings as the Capitals, and they have one of the best rosters in the Metro Division. Washington has the ingredients to challenge the defending Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and get Ovechkin one more ring before he rides off into the sunset.

#2596. Josh Hart admits he’s ‘not in a good head space’as his Knicks struggles mount

INDIANAPOLIS — Josh Hart's issues aren't exclusive to his shot. The Knicks veteran said he's mentally struggling to start a disappointing season, and he doesn't know how to break out of it.

"Wish I could tell you," Hart said. "Don't know. Right now I'm not in a good head space and I got to figure out how to improve that. And improve my play."

Asked what that meant, Hart, who is shooting just 36 percent on the season, said, "Just mentally. Got to be better mentally. Got to figure stuff out."

Josh Hart of the New York Knicks shoots a 3-pointer against the Indiana Pacers in Indianapolis on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images

Hart finished scoreless Friday night and was benched for the entire fourth quarter of a 106-104 loss to the Pacers, among the low points of a season that has never been on track for the 31-year-old.

He's up for an extension, but the Knicks put out a statement in October declaring they're shutting down all negotiations, including Hart's and Karl-Anthony Towns'.

Hart revealed Friday that he suffered a calf injury before training camp, which set back his conditioning. He then hurt his ankle and missed three games.

The Knicks are stacked with wings and guards, creating congestion and sporadic playing time. Mikal Bridges has also been benched, as coach Mike Brown leaned on Landry Shamet and Miles McBride.

Brown acknowledged that finding time for Bridges and Hart could be difficult.

Josh Hart, left, speaks with New York Knicks teammate Mikal Bridges during a game against the Indiana Pacers in Indianapolis on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images

"There are several different ways you can look at it," Hart said. "You can look at it, if they have it going, cool. Good. You could look at it like, 'OK, maybe something else has to change.'"

Hart didn't specify the "change," but logic indicates he meant a trade. Three years ago, Leon Rose faced a similar conundrum. Too many guards, not enough minutes.

So Rose traded two — RJ Barrett and Immanuel Quickley — for a bigger forward in OG Anunoby.

Beginning Sunday, the Knicks face Barrett and Quickley twice in three days in Toronto, while Hart tries to find a better headspace.
