Impact: Adonai Mitchell could operate as the Jets' No. 1 wide receiver in his albeit volatile downfield role.

In Week 9, Cooper injured the same ankle that he hurt earlier this year, but he practiced in a limited capacity to begin Week 10. Despite drawing the questionable tag, he is expected to play.

Impact: Cooper is on track to play and warrants FLEX treatment against the Bills.

Mitchell is listed as questionable for Week 10 but is expected to play.Impact: Minimal. The downfield threat brings a wide range of outcomes on a weekly basis and makes for one of the more "yolo" starts in fantasy circles.

Jackson returned from an ankle injury in Week 8 and made it all of one offensive snap before suffering a thumb injury that is likely to sideline him for the remainder of the regular season.

Impact: Jackson's absence is the biggest hit to the fantasy value of alpha receiver Zay Flowers, who falls to a mid-range WR2 in rest of season rankings. Recent signee Jacoby Brissett is expected to start under center in Week 10.

Huntley suffered a season-ending turf toe injury in the team's Week 8 loss to the Bills.

Smythe suffered a torn Achilles in the team's Week 4 win over the Titans. His season is done.

Impact: It was Matt Hibner who saw the largest increase in snaps following Smythe's departure in Week 4, making it unlikely we see veteran Mark Andrews in a more robust role.

The Bengals placed Iosivas on injured reserve in Week 3. The team activated his 21-day practice window this week but he is listed as doubtful to play in Week 10 against the Steelers.

Impact: Wide receivers Colbie Young and Dohnte Meyers will duke it out for the No. 3 wide receiver role for at least the next four weeks. Meyers can be added in 14-team leagues, though his upside is questionable.

All suffered a torn ACL in Week 7. He was placed on injured reserve Tuesday and will miss the remainder of the regular season.

Impact: All loses yet another season in devastating fashion after suffering his third torn ACL. His absence could provide a slight uptick in snap rate and route participation for Mike Gesicki, although he will be a difficult weekly start for as long as both Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins remain healthy.

Fannin played through the injury in Week 9, but did not enter the box score until overtime. He was limited to begin Week 10 and removed from the injury report Friday.

Boston did not practice to begin Week 10, ultimately drawing the questionable tag.

Impact: Boston continues to deal with lower-leg injuries, but he played effectively last week. If he cannot face the Texans in Week 10, KC Concepcion and Fannin would benefit.

Impact: He will be eligible to return after four games missed.

Pittman was limited on Wednesday before being seen using a scooter in the locker room after practice. It was then revealed that Pittman aggravated his foot injury. The Steelers placed him on injured reserve late in Week 5. The Steelers did not open his 21-day practice window after their Week 9 bye.

Impact: Pittman's potential return could lower Germie Bernard's target share.

Wilson departed in the second half of Week 5 with a finger injury and is reportedly looking at a multi-game absence. He was ruled out for Week 6 on Friday and placed on injured reserve on Saturday.

The veteran tight end was added to the injury report Saturday with an illness, listed as questionable.

Impact: We expect Freiermuth to play through the illness despite the late addition to the injury report. Darnell Washington could be a name to keep on fantasy radars, should Freiermuth miss.

Marks was limited to begin Week 10 but was removed from the injury report Friday.

Dell was limited to begin Week 10 but removed from the injury report Friday.

Impact: Dell led the team with nine targets last week. He may have his work slightly scaled back this week, but he remains FLEX-viable.

Harrison was limited to begin Week 10. He was ruled out Friday.

Impact: Hamstring injuries can be tricky for wide receivers. Kayshon Boutte and Xavier Hutchinson would mildly benefit with Harrison sidelined.

Noel suffered a turf toe injury in Week 7. The Texans placed him on injured reserve in Week 8. He is expected to miss the remainder of the regular season.

Impact: Tank Dell and recent acquisition Marvin Harrison Jr. would be in line to benefit. Harrison should be added in 12-team formats.

Head coach DeMeco Ryans said in Week 5 that Montgomery is "week-to-week" with a groin injury. He remains sidelined early in Week 10 and was ultimately ruled out.

Impact: Woody Marks is a low-end RB2/FLEX.

The Texans placed Jordan on injured reserve in Week 7.

Impact: Jordan prevented Marks from handling a full-time role in Week 6. Dare Ogunbowale will probably do the same while Montgomery is sidelined.

Higgins saw his 2026 season taken from him due to a torn ACL suffered in camp.

Impact: It's a massive blow to a Texans team that was counting on Higgins taking another step forward in his Sophomore campaign. The team traded for Kayshon Boutte in the wake of the injury and then added Marvin Harrison Jr. in a deal with the Cardinals ahead of Week 6.

Pierce aggravated the injury that required offseason surgery in Week 2. The Colts placed him on injured reserve in Week 3. He will attempt to avoid surgery by rehabbing his injured heel. Head coach Shane Steichen said he is unsure whether Pierce will play again this season.

Impact: Tyler Warren is the de facto top option through the air for the remainder of the season.

Tuten played in Week 9's Thursday Night Football after failing to practice leading up to the game. He did not practice the following Wednesday but was removed from the injury report Friday and will play in Week 10.

Impact: Tuten saw his workload managed in the second half of a blowout win but appears to have escaped without aggravating either injury. Fantasy managers will want to track his status coming out of the mini-bye.

Rodriguez played through the injury in Week 9 and remained limited early in Week 10. He was removed from the injury report Friday and will play against the Titans.

Meyers played through the injury in Week 9 and sat out the following Wednesday. He was removed from the injury report Friday and will play against the Titans.

Impact: Meyers is a touchdown-dependent FLEX.

Carnell Tate - WR (shoulder)Tate remains sidelined following the Titans' Week 9 bye. He was ruled out for Week 10 Friday.

Impact: This could be consequential. Chimere Dike stepped into the vacated role almost to a tee and brings viable FLEX upside in a pass-funnel matchup against the Jaguars.

As of Week 10, Spears has been sidelined since Week 7. He is listed as questionable for Week 10.

Impact: Fantasy managers will want to confirm his status 90 minutes prior to first kick.

Waddle suffered a concussion in the team's Week 9 win over the Panthers.

Impact: The team's Week 10 bye should afford Waddle enough time to return without missing a game.

Harvey popped on the injury report Thursday with a knee injury and was ruled out for Week 8 on Friday. He was placed on injured reserve Saturday and will miss the next four weeks, at minimum.

Impact: Jonah Coleman is an RB2, operating as the team's starter.

Walker was added to the injury report Friday after missing practice with groin tightness, ultimately ruled out for Week 10 against the Falcons.Impact: Walker's absence shocks the fantasy landscape for Week 10, with Emmett Johnson now in line to serve as a true workhorse back in a run-funnel matchup against the Falcons. Fantasy managers will want to add and start Johnson immediately as a viable RB2 with RB1 upside.

Mahomes suffered an elbow injury to his throwing arm in the team's Week 9 win over the Jets. He is practicing in full for Week 10 against the Falcons.

Impact: Pain management could lead to reduced throwing volume for Mahomes. Backup quarterback Justin Fields (neck) is practicing in full as well.

Thornton suffered a devastating ankle injury due to a hip-drop tackle in Week 4. He is reportedly set to undergo surgery within the week and will miss 12-16 weeks.

Impact: The team has lost all ability to attack downfield without Thornton, meaning our fantasy interest should be confined to those with expected volume.

The Raiders emerged from their Week 9 loss to the 49ers absent any fantasy-relevant injuries.

Njoku is reportedly set to see his 21-day practice window opened in the coming days. He was limited to begin Week 10 before drawing the questionable tag.

Impact: Minimal. The Chargers have been the most disappointing offense in the league through the halfway point of the season.

McConkey reportedly experienced back spasms during warmups for Week 9 and ultimately did not play. He is listed as questionable for Week 10.

Impact: McConkey would be a WR3 if active, although fantasy managers are likely better off making alternate arrangements considering the timing of the Chargers' game.

Ferguson departed the team's Week 9 win with an ankle injury. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Monday that the veteran tight end is "expected to miss time." He was ruled out for Week 10 Friday.

Impact: Brevin Span-Ford is on hand to handle primary tight end duties. He is not a recommended streaming option outside of the deepest leagues.

Pickens missed Week 9 with a hamstring injury. He was limited to begin Week 10 before being removed from the injury report Friday.

Impact: Back to business as usual for the Cowboys for their Week 10 showdown against the 49ers. Pickens is an upside WR3 in a difficult matchup on the perimeter.

Davis was placed on injured reserve and will miss the remainder of the 2026 season.

Impact: The Cowboys released both Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah at roster cuts and now have only Emari Demercado on the active roster behind starter Javonte Williams. Expect Israel Abanikanda to be elevated to the active roster from the practice squad for Week 2, while Williams appears likely to see all the work he can handle against the Commanders. Williams is a locked-in RB1.

The team sent Goodson to injured reserve Saturday.Impact: The Cowboys have struggled with depth in the backfield all season, which takes another blow in the absence of Goodson. Israel Abanikanda was signed to the active roster and will serve as the primary change of pace option behind Javonte Williams in the immediate future. Williams remains a locked-in RB2 with one of the more robust roles in the league.

Dart injured his MCL, PCL and meniscus on the team's first possession of Monday Night Football against the Rams. He will undergo surgery to address the MCL and meniscus and miss the rest of the regular season. Giants head coach John Harbaugh said it is possible for Dart to return in the postseason, although this is unlikely.

Impact: Backup Jameis Winston was benched in favor of recent acquisition J.J. McCarthy in the second half of their loss to the Saints. Head coach John Harbaugh confirmed McCarthy as the starter for Week 7.

Skattebo will play in Week 10 after sitting out in Week 9.

Impact: Skattebo is back in the RB2 ranks against the Commanders.

McCarthy was in and out of the lineup in Week 9 after a painful hip pointer. He will play in Week 10 against the Commanders.

Impact: McCarthy is QB2-viable on Thursday night.

Barkley should continue to play through the ailments after being active in Week 9.

Pierce was injured on a kick return in the fourth quarter of the team's Week 7 loss to the Cowboys. He was placed on injured reserve the following Wednesday.

Smith has repeatedly aggravated the hamstring strain he initially injured in August. Smith was ruled out for Week 7 on Saturday, and as of early in Week 9, he remains sidelined. Both Smith and Dontayvion Wicks were ruled out for Week 9 on Friday.

Impact: Wide receivers Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) and Britain Covey (knee) remain sidelined as well. All three could be held out through the Eagles' Week 10 bye. Tight end Dallas Goedert and Makai Lemon benefit.

Team doctors discovered a blood clot in Hurts' calf. He was ruled out for Week 6 and could be looking at an extended absence. He was placed on injured reserve on Saturday after more clots were found in his lungs.

Impact: Hurts is currently sidelined indefinitely. Tanner McKee enters the starting lineup under center following the release of Andy Dalton. The Philadelphia offense could be in trouble in the immediate future considering the sheer number of injuries.

Shipley reportedly suffered a partial tear of the plantar fascia in his foot in Week 5. He is expected to miss multiple weeks.

McLaurin suffered a season-ending patellar tendon rupture in Week 6.

Impact: Stefon Diggs will likely serve as the de facto No. 1 wide receiver moving forward.

Lane suffered a dislocated ankle and fracture in Week 4 and is likely done for the season.

Croskey-Merritt was unable to practice this week and ruled out for Week 6 against the 49ers. The team placed him on injured reserve on Saturday.

Impact: Expect Rachaad White to fill in as the primary rusher, with Austin Ekeler on hand to soak up primary change of pace duties. White can be started as a viable FLEX option while Ekeler is likely best left on fantasy benches.

McNichols suffered a foot injury in Week 8 and was placed on injured reserve in Week 9.

Impact: Rachaad White and veteran Austin Ekeler are suddenly the only two healthy backs on the Washington roster, neither of whom is an overly exciting fantasy option on a struggling offense. White is the preferred option and could be started as a viable FLEX, should McNichols miss time.

Burks did not play in Week 9. He was cleared to play in Week 10's Thursday Night Football game despite logging on limited practice this week, on Tuesday.

Impact: Burks could be a decoy. Antonio Williams is limited to FLEX status until he proves otherwise.

Head coach Ben Johnson labeled Monangai as "day-to-day" with a thumb injury suffered in Week 4, but he was later revealed to have suffered a turf toe injury as well. Monangai remains sidelined as of Week 9's Wednesday practice. He did not play in Week 9.

Impact: D'Andre Swift is an RB1, should Monangai miss another game. Roschon Johnson can be stashed.

Kmet suffered a season-ending knee injury in the team's Thursday Night Football win over the Patriots.

Impact: Expect Sam Roush to serve as the team's TE2 for the remainder of the season, while second-year tight end Colston Loveland should continue his recent ascension back into TE1 territory.

Goff's play may have been impacted by the injury in-game last week, though it is tough to say for sure. Hopefully he upgrades to full participation on Thursday. He was limited on Wednesday.

St. Brown was limited on Wednesday after playing through the injury in Week 9. He is once again listed as questionable for Week 10.

Pacheco was placed on injured reserve to start the season. General Manager Brad Holmes said he "hopes Pacheco returns this season."

Impact: Well, that doesn't sound great. There appears to be something more insidious going on with Pacheco's back than initially thought. Lions coach Dan Campbell said running backs Jacob Saylors and Sione Vaki could split touches behind Jahmyr Gibbs. Saylors appears to be the first player up. Gibbs handled an absurd 34 opportunities, of 37 total running back opportunities, in the team's Week 1, overtime win over the Saints

Jacobs suffered a fractured finger in the team's Week 9 win over the Patriots. He will miss two-to-three weeks after undergoing surgery.

Impact: Kaleb Johnson is reportedly the first in line for lead back duties in his absence.

Reed suffered a scary-looking neck injury that required stabilization in the team's Week 2 win over the Jets. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said on Tuesday that it is "way too early" to determine whether Reed will play again in 2026. That said, he was not placed on injured reserve ahead of their Week 3 contest. He will reportedly undergo surgery.

Impact: Beyond the football implications, it is good to hear Reed avoided any life-altering injuries in Week 2. Skyy Moore and Bo Melton are likely to soak up additional snaps, although volume is most likely to concentrate on Christian Watson, Matthew Golden, and Tucker Kraft.

Brooks suffered an ankle injury in the team's Week 4 win over the Buccaneers. The Packers designated him to return from injured reserve in Week 9 and he is listed as questionable for Week 10.

Impact: Brooks will rotate in on passing downs upon his return for pass-protection duties.

Impact: Murray can be dropped. Carson Wentz (ankle) is also ailing.

Hockenson did not practice on Wednesday. He was ruled out for Week 10 Friday.

Impact: Jauan Jennings remains sidelined and Jordan Addison is listed a questionable after banging his thumb in practice Friday. Justin Jefferson could see all the volume he can handle, although his per-target efficiency likely improves with Addison on the field in a downfield role.

Robinson was placed on injured reserve on Saturday.

Impact: In a shocking development, Robinson went from limited showings in practice with a questionable designation for Week 9 to injured reserve, with the potential that the veteran backup aggravated his ailment sometime during practice to end the week. He will miss the next four games, at minimum. Khalil Herbert should continue as the top change-of-pace option behind Bijan Robinson, the former of whom is not fantasy-viable.

Branch was ruled out for Week 9 against the Bengals early in the week. He remains sidelined in Week 10.

Impact: Drake London, Bijan Robinson and Kyle Pitts should continue dominating targets.

Brooks aggravated the groin injury that forced him to miss the end of camp. The Panthers placed him on injured reserve in Week 3. The Panthers designated him to return in Week 10. He was ruled out for Week 10 Friday after a week of limited sessions.

Impact: Chuba Hubbard remains in the volume-driven RB1 tier.

The Saints opened Etienne's 21-day practice window in Week 10. He was limited on Wednesday. Reports from Saturday indicate the team is likely to activate Etienne ahead of their Week 10 meeting with the Panthers.

Impact: Etienne likely returns to a timeshare with Audric Estime and Alvin Kamara, none of whom warrant fantasy consideration.

McMillan suffered a sprained PCL in his first game action of the season in Week 3. The team placed him on injured reserve Monday, with an expected absence of 6-8 weeks.

Impact: Not much change considering he made his season debut in Week 3, although rookie Ted Hurst should remain in the starting lineup.

The team placed Love on injured reserve after yet another ankle injury sustained in Week 8.

Impact: Bam Knight (concussion) resumed practicing in Week 10. Tyler Allgeier likely returns to a receiving/rotational rushing role.

Brooks had emergency surgery on his wrist and will miss the remainder of the regular season.

Impact: The team signed veteran Zay Jones Tuesday in an associated move. Expect volume to continue to remain heavily concentrated on Michael Wilson and Trey McBride. Elijah Higgins is notable for DFS purposes.

Minshew is feared to have torn his UCL in the team's Week 9 loss to the Seahawks.

Impact: Minshew appears likely to be placed on injured reserve in the coming days, leaving rookie Carson Beck to start under center for the remainder of the season.

Wilson suffered a neck injury in Week 9 that will end his 2026 season.

Impact: The Cardinals are now without their starting quarterback, second-string quarterback, alpha wide receiver, secondary and tertiary wide receiver, and starting running back as they head into the second half of a lost season. Trey McBride should soak up all the volume he can handle, with that volume now coming from rookie Carson Beck.

Ferguson appeared to be on track to be activated from injured reserve after logging a full practice to end the week, but was ruled out for Week 9 with a new hamstring injury. He will miss multiple games.

Impact: Fantasy managers will have to continue to wait for the return of Ferguson.

Impact: The Rams will employ run-heavy game plans in the coming weeks.

Nacua suffered PCL and MCL sprains, plus a turf toe injury, on the final play from scrimmage in the team's Week 9 win over the Commanders. Nacua was placed on injured reserve Friday.

Evans aggravated his Achilles injury in Week 6 and is expected to "miss some time." He remains sidelined early in Week 10 and was ruled out Friday.

Samuel suffered a hamstring injury in the team's Week 5 win over the Seahawks. He resumed practicing in Week 10 and told reporters he is "ready" to play.

Impact: Samuel would return to the high-end FLEX tier if active.

Kirk was limited on Wednesday. He was ruled out for Week 9 on Friday and placed on injured reserve on Saturday.

Stribling suffered an ankle injury in the team's Week 1 win over the Rams. The 49ers placed him on injured reserve in Week 2 after he underwent surgery to repair a deltoid ligament tear. He is expected to return in 10 weeks.

Pearsall was placed on season-ending injured reserve.

Impact: Pearsall will miss the entirety of the 2026 season.

The Seahawks ruled out Darnold for Week 9 on Wednesday. He was also ruled out for Week 10.

Impact: Drew Lock (elbow/oblique) will be limited in practice this week before starting against the Raiders. He is a QB2.

Shaheed injured his knee during a collision with teammate Jaxon Smith-Njigba in Week 7. He is practicing in full for Week 10 against the Raiders and was removed from the injury report Friday.

Impact: Shaheed is likely just a touchdown-dependent FLEX.

#2562. NHL Power Rankings: Oilers fly out of the starting gates behind Connor McDavid, Evan Bouchard

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

How many times in recent history have the Edmonton Oilers dug themselves an early hole only to surge back toward the top of the Pacific Division standings? It doesn't look like that surge will be necessary in 2026-27.

I had serious reservations about the Mike Babcock hire -- and I still do -- but Edmonton has been mauling opponents early. The Oilers are off to a 5-0-1 start while posting a plus-11 goal differential. Each of the team's wins has come by at least two goals.

As you might expect, Connor McDavid, Leon Draisaitl and Evan Bouchard are driving the bus in oil country. McDavid leads the NHL with 17 points, and Draisaitl is in double-digits with 11 points of his own, but Bouchard has been the star of the show early.

Bouchard has always been an offensive machine, but he's hit another level. He's tallied six goals and eight assists, and his 14 points leads all defensemen by a comfortable margin. The most impressive part of Bouchard's game to this point has been his five-on-five impacts. With Bouchard on the ice, the Oilers have outscored opponents 15-2, per Natural Stat Trick.

With Zach Hyman and Ryan Nugent-Hopkins out of the lineup, the Oilers haven't missed a beat thanks to its trio of superstars.

As the Oilers challenge the defending champs for the No. 1 spot, here are the updated NHL Power Rankings.

#2561. JJ Buchanan injury update: Michigan WR in tears after getting hurt

Michigan football may have lost leading receiver JJ Buchanan to injury in the second quarter of the Week 11 game against Oregon at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Nov. 14.

Buchanan seemed to be favoring his shoulder and broke down in tears as he hugged his wide receivers coach on the sideline at Autzen Stadium.

Michigan (5-4, 2-4 Big Ten) was trailing No. 19 Oregon when Buchanan exited with the injury.

Buchanan entered the game leading the Wolverines with 40 catches for 646 yards, a 16.1 yards per catch average, and five touchdowns despite poor quarterback play.

After the game against the Ducks on Saturday, the Wolverines will head home to host UCLA at the Big House before hitting the road again for the final game against Ohio State.

#2560. Michael Pittman Jr. says he feels healthy enough to return

The Pittsburgh Steelers made no trades ahead of Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, despite a clear need at wide receiver. Although the Steelers were interested in Tennessee's Calvin Ridley and Jacksonville's Brian Thomas Jr., a trade never materialized. While the receiver room has a bleak outlook right now, one of the Steelers' highest paid receivers seems close to making his return from injured reserve.

Steelers veteran wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. has been out since Week 4 after suffering a plantar fasciitis injury. Still, it seems like his return could come sooner rather than later.

"It feels good, and today was probably my best day yet," Pittman told Brendan Howe of Steelers Now on Thursday. "Yesterday was good, today was even better, so definitely trending the right way.… I would love the opportunity to play this week, but that's out of my control. I definitely let them know today that I thought it was good."

Pittman Jr. remains on injured reserve, with the Steelers yet to open his 21-day practice window. The receiver was seen working off to the side this week and even ran during warmups. Although Pittman Jr. will be out this week against Cincinnati, the receiver feels healthy enough to go.

The Steelers acquired Pittman Jr. in a trade with the Indianapolis Colts this past March. The receiver has appeared in just three games so far this season, recording seven catches for 89 yards in those contests.

The last time the Los Angeles Dodgers lost the first two games of a best-of-seven playoff series, they were unable to recover as they were defeated in six by the Atlanta Braves in the 2021 National League Championship Series. Just like in that matchup, the Dodgers dropped the first two contests of this year's NLCS on the road.

Los Angeles avoided going down 0-3 five years ago with a home victory, and if it hopes to keep alive its chances of becoming the first NL team in Major League Baseball history to win three consecutive World Series titles, it likely will need a triumph at Dodger Stadium on Wednesday as it hosts the Milwaukee Brewers at 8 p.m. ET for Game 3 of the 2026 NLCS.

The Dodgers were the first team to repeat as world champions since the New York Yankees won three straight championships from 1998-2000 when they beat the Toronto Blue Jays in seven games in the 2025 World Series. They knocked off Atlanta in four games in this year's NL Division Series but were edged by Milwaukee 2-1 in the opener of the NLCS and fell 7-4 in Game 2 as Tarik Skubal and 2025 World Series MVP Yoshinobu Yamamoto had their issues on the mound.

Los Angeles now turns to Blake Snell, who lasted only 3 2/3 innings in his start against the Braves in Game 2 of the NLDS. The two-time Cy Young Award winner allowed just one run and three hits but issued five walks in that outing.

However, Snell was masterful when he faced the Brewers in Game 1 of the 2025 NLCS. The 33-year-old lefthander limited Milwaukee to one single and registered 10 strikeouts over eight scoreless innings as the Dodgers recorded a 2-1 victory.

The Brewers attempt to move within one win of the second World Series appearance in franchise history and first as members of the NL behind southpaw Robert Gasser. The 27-year-old rookie made his first career postseason start in Game 4 of the NLDS against the San Diego Padres and pitched relatively well, giving up one run and three hits over four innings.

But Gasser had no success in two meetings with the Dodgers during the regular season as he went 0-2 while surrendering seven runs and 12 hits across 10 2/3 innings. Andy Pages went 4-for-5 against Gasser with a double, a homer and two RBI while Kyle Tucker was 3-for-6 with a triple and a solo blast.

#2558. No-call on Pacers' late turnover against Knicks was incorrect per NBA

The turnover that nearly cost the Pacers their upset of the defending champion Knicks on Friday night should have been called a foul, the NBA ruled Saturday.

The Pacers had the ball with 5.0 seconds to go and a 106-104 lead with the ball sideline out of bounds. All-Star forward Pascal Siakam tried to throw a pass to point guard Andrew Nembhard but Knicks wing Mikal Bridges appeared to hold him back and kept him from grabbing the ball. Knicks forward O.G. Anunoby grabbed the loose ball and called timeout with 2.8 seconds to go to advance the ball. In the scramble, Pacers forward Aaron Nesmith injured his hand. The Knicks had a chance to tie the game on the last possession but center Karl-Anthony Towns missed a game-tying jumper.

No foul was called against Bridges on the play, the close score necessitated a last-two-minute report to be released. According to the report, the play was ruled an incorrect no call because "Bridges (NYK) wraps an arm around Nembhard's (IND) waist while attempting to get to the pass, affecting Nembhard's SQBR (speed, quickness, battle and rhythm)."

The league also ruled that an incorrect call was issued when Nembhard was called for a kicked ball violation with 1:22 left in the game.

One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

#2555. Group of retired MLB umpires, including Joe West, file lawsuit alleging they are owed more than $2 million

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Former MLB umpire Joe West is part of a group of five retired umpires who are suing their pension plan and alleging they have been underpaid by the plan, the Associated Press reports. West, along with Tom Hallion, Gerry Davis, Larry Vanover, and Jerry Layne, filed the suit in late September in federal court in New York.

The suit alleges that the five umpires have been underpaid by the pension plan by more than $2 million. According to the AP, the suit "was filed against the American Leagues and National Leagues of Professional Baseball Clubs Retirement Income Plan for Umpires and that entity's retirement committee." The five umpires claim their benefits were not calculated correctly and therefore should receive additional money.

West, 74, retired from umpiring in MLB in 2021 after umpiring more than 5,000 games at the highest level starting in 1976. The man they called "Cowboy Joe" umpired a record 5,460 games in all, was known as a colorful figure in the sport and sometimes even a source of controversy.

In 2021, West won more than $500,000 in damages as the result of a defamation suit against former MLB player Paul Lo Duca after Lo Duca alleged during a podcast that West would "open up the strike zone" for reliever Billy Wagner in exchange for driving one of Wagner's vintage cars.

West referenced his "history with lawsuits" on Thursday. From the AP:

West said that when he brought up the issue to the retirement committee, he was offered a relatively small sum. West said MLB senior vice president and chief employment counsel Steven Gonzalez told him: "If you don't like the number, sue us."

"Does Steve Gonzalez not know my history with dealing with lawsuits?" West said.

Like West, Davis also retired after the 2021 season while Hallion umpired through the 2022 season and Layne and Vanover stepped away after the 2024 campaign. The five sued as individuals and did not involve the umpires' union, their lawyer, Paul B. Holmes, said, per the AP.

A pretrial conference in the case is scheduled for Dec. 11.

#2552. Ex-Guardians catcher Bo Naylor testifies in defense of Emmanuel Clase, Luis Ortiz in MLB pitch-rigging trial

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Former Cleveland Guardians catcher Bo Naylor on Thursday testified in federal court that he perceived nothing untoward about disputed pitches thrown by former All-Star closer Emmanuel Clase and his former Guardians teammate Luis Ortiz, ESPN reports.

Naylor, who played five seasons for the Guardians, appeared as a witness for the defense in the ongoing federal trial in which prosecutors allege that Clase and Ortiz rigged multiple pitches for the benefit of co-conspiring bettors. In Clase's case, he's alleged to have done so in 17 games across a two-year period beginning in May 2023. Naylor, now a member of the Milwaukee Brewers, was catcher for some of Clase's disputed appearances during that span, including seven of the 18 pitches he's alleged to have rigged.

Naylor, a defense witness, was shown video replays of some of the pitches the government alleges were predetermined by Clase or Ortiz as part of the scheme. Naylor was behind the plate for many of them and said they looked like common sliders outside the strike zone. He said the scouting reports on the hitters Ortiz faced during the two pitches in question indicated that sliders low and away would be a "weapon."

In November 2025, Clase and Ortiz were indicted by the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of New York. According to the Department of Justice, both pitchers "agreed in advance with their co-conspirators to throw specific types of pitches and speeds of pitches." The Department of Justice alleged that the pair made at least $450,000 by rigging outings and throwing specific pitches to benefit bettors who wagered on the outcomes of those pitches.

Both Clase and Ortiz pleaded not guilty to those charges in November of last year. Clase and Ortiz have been on administrative leave since late June 2025 while Major League Baseball investigates. MLB has the authority to discipline the pitchers regardless of how the criminal trial plays out.

The pair could face up to 65 years in prison if convicted on the charges of wire fraud conspiracy, honest services wire fraud conspiracy, conspiracy to influence sporting contests by bribery, and money laundering conspiracy.

#2549. Here are 4 ways OKC Thunder can fix current struggles amid losing streak

After Shai Gilgeous-Alexander missed on two chances to hit a game-winner, the Oklahoma City Thunder are in newish territory. They're amid a three-game losing streak for the first time in years. This is their first lengthy skid since April 2023. Yeah, it's been that long.

If nothing else, OKC's season-long four-game road trip has been a humbling experience. Riding high from a previous four-game winning streak, the Thunder have come to grips with their new NBA reality. Your ceiling as a team is severely limited if you're missing three of your four best players — plus other important pieces.

I mean, yeah, duh. But for the first time in years, the Thunder are no longer a regular-season win machine. They're mortal. Like the rest of the NBA. How can OKC still salvage this season? Here are four quick fixes that should serve as duct tape until help arrives:

Transforming his shot diet to be more perimeter-friendly, Gilgeous-Alexander caught flak in recent days. The Thunder need him to be the superb-efficient 30-plus point scorer he's been over the past four seasons. Not just someone who will get you 25-ish points on decent efficiency. The 28-year-old has fallen in love with the mid-range and outside jumpers. That explains why his driving numbers are down. Which also explains why his free-throw numbers have dipped, too.

Two losses to the Portland Trail Blazers put Gilgeous-Alexander's junky shot diet at the forefront. I guess he got the message. He returned to his vintage form in a loss to the LA Clippers. He had 40 points on 15-of-26 shooting and shot 8-of-11 on free throws. He only went 2-of-4 from 3. Even though he missed two chances to hit go-ahead shots in the final 36 seconds, you love the shot process he had.

Look — Gilgeous-Alexander entered the year with ambitions of an easier workload. The Thunder highlighted an off-ball role. He had hoped to save his legs for the NBA playoffs by getting away from a physically-taxing playstyle of being a drive-heavy scorer. But those plans are out the window. The sky actually fell this time. He needs to be a one-man show every night to salvage this year. Whatever that looks like.

The endgame is Chet Holmgren. The Thunder know for a fact he'll be back this regular season. Probably around New Year's as he's still in the early stages of an 8-to-10-week timetable. The All-NBA talent received a biological treatment to address a small torn patellar tendon. He's the big fish. And who knows? Maybe, best-case scenario, Jalen Williams and/or Cason Wallace miraculously return, too. OKC left the door open for a reason.

But the Thunder won't have to wait long to get additional help. Nikola Topic returned in OKC's loss to the Clippers. He missed the first dozen games recovering from back surgery that took longer than anticipated to return from. There's also a litter of other NBA guys on the precipice of returning.

Ajay Mitchell has missed the last two games with an ankle sprain. That surely won't cost him more time — if any. Jaylin Williams has missed five in a row with back spasms. Hopefully, he's using the time off to get in better NBA shape. He's had a slow start to his year. And then there's the ever-mysterious Thomas Sorber. I mean, he has to be back soonish, right? He's participated in intense pregame warmups for weeks now. I think he's on the doorstep of making his long-anticipated NBA debut after a year and a half.

Since Alex Caruso joined the Thunder, he's been famously bubble-wrapped in the regular season. He's started four games in just three seasons. His minutes have only eclipsed 20 minutes per night just once — this year. You're just not afforded that luxury right now. The 32-year-old remains one of your most impactful players. It's time to go all out.

The Thunder have an eye-popping plus-25.4 net rating when Caruso is on the floor in 204 minutes this season. That number sinks to minus-7.7 net rating when he's off the floor in 420 minutes. That's a plus-33.1 swing. I mean, you can't have that sitting on the bench in a reserved role. Especially with how dire things are right now with their glued-together rotation.

I think it's time to throw caution to the wind. At least, for the next couple of months. Caruso must be a full-time starter. He's proven before to be capable of the workload. He's the sole healthy high-end point-of-attack defender you have. The Thunder need the All-Defensive talent to match up with the opposition's top perimeter scorers at the start of games. Or risk falling behind from the jump — ala when Darius Garland absolutely carved up Jared McCain in OKC's loss to the Clippers.

The Thunder need to find NBA-quality talent. And fast. The most sure-fire way of at least trying that? Bringing in new two-way guys. I mean, that's kinda the whole point of that semi-standard contract, right? To see if you can find hidden gems in the G League? Right now, I think we can confidently say that's not really the case with this crop of OKC's two-way talent.

Micah Peavy is the best of the bunch. He can defend. But the jumper and his offense are a lost cause. His playing time has dwindled because of it. As controversial as this might be, I actually like what Josh Dix brings to the table. Sure, he's a theoretical-3-and-D player, but his defense and energy have been a nice touch. I can't blame him too much for how many crunch-time minutes he played in OKC's loss to the Clippers. That falls on the coaching staff.

But, Brooks Barnhizer? I think he's the easiest to replace. He's been out of the rotation for weeks. He's not playing with the G League's OKC Blue to get developmental reps. What exactly are we doing here? You can't just waste a valuable roster spot like that right now. The Thunder have to bring in new blood. Just for the sake of change. Even if the odds are astronomically small that somebody in the G League will be a season-saver.

Young, 27, has always been a superlative defender. He unlocked a new level on offense this season, particularly in the second half, when he hit .301 with a .385 on-base percentage. Young had been speculated as a trade candidate since last offseason, but the new extension locks him in as part of Washington's long-term core.

#2545. Five under-the-radar MLB free agents who could make a big impact next season

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The 2026-27 MLB offseason is a little more than a week old now and we're still waiting for the first big trade or free agent signing. That isn't unusual, though. The hot stove, like the regular season, is a marathon, not a sprint. A lockout is expected when the collective bargaining agreement ends at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1, and there should be a flurry of activity before then.

We ranked the offseason's top 50 free agents, and although it is not a great class, there are dozens of quality players available. You just have to know where to look. Here now are five players who did not rank among our top 50 free agents, but would nonetheless be good options and solid pickups for teams that want to raise their floor and improve their supporting cast.

It was a tale of two seasons for the 29-year-old Bryan Abreu, who had a 5.81 ERA before the All-Star break and a 1.71 ERA after. The under-the-hood estimators, like FIP and xERA, were better in the second half as well, though Abreu lost close to 2 mph off his fastball this year and, not coincidentally, a whole bunch of swings and misses. Abreu is third in appearances and second in innings among relievers since 2022 and it's possible the workload is catching up to him. There's still enough bat-missing ability and late-inning experience here for Abreu to contribute to a contender's bullpen. It just might happen as a seventh-inning guy moving forward, not as the Moment of Truth™ reliever who pitches in the game's biggest moments.

If you're looking for a bottom of the order guy who will take walks and give you 10-15 home runs, that's J.P. Crawford. His defense, specifically his range and arm, has slipped so much in his early 30s that he's no longer a viable shortstop, though he played 33 games at third base this past season. I like him better at second base, but third base works too. Crawford gets on-base at a decent clip and won't strike out excessively, plus he's long been regarded as an excellent teammate and grade-A clubhouse guy. It seems like his time with the Mariners is over and it's for the best. Crawford can go elsewhere, play a new position, and just be part of the lineup rather than one of the faces of the franchise.

Due to injury and ineffectiveness, it looked like Sean Newcomb was on his way out of baseball two years ago. He then reinvented himself as a sinker/curveball guy and carved out a nice second phase to his career as a workhorse utility reliever who won't beat himself with walks (an early career bugaboo) and will limit hard contact in the air. Newcomb, 33, worked at least 90 innings the last two seasons while pitching in every possible role. He closed out games, worked high leverage as a setup guy, soaked up innings in long relief, and opened a few times as well. Newcomb is likely miscast as a go-to bullpen option, though he can be a valuable third or fourth option for a contender. The utility reliever is all the rage these days and Newcomb fits the profile to a T.

Now 35, Emilio Pagán was sensational after returning from a hamstring injury in July, pitching to a 1.88 ERA with 34 strikeouts and only five walks in his final 28 ⅔ innings. The downside is the same as it's always been: Pagán is exceptionally home run prone (career 1.51 HR/9), which is a bad trait for a late-inning reliever who pitches almost exclusively in close games. His fastball remains firm, though, and his splitter is an elite swing-and-miss pitch that allows him to neutralize righties and lefties. As long as you're willing to live with the home run risk, Pagán remains a capable high-leverage reliever, one who is not out of place pitching important innings for a contending team.

Platoon DHs are not the hottest commodity, but Joc Pederson fills the role about as well as anyone in the game. He's a left-handed hitter, so he's on the heavy side of the platoon, and he authored a .245/.338/.496 line with terrific ball-tracking data (exit velocity, etc.) against righties. If you must play him in the field, Pederson can stand in right field or at first base for about six innings before being subbed out for a defensive replacement. He's essentially a bat-only player, though. Pederson will turn 35 in April and he's still a powerful and productive hitter against righties and an elite clubhouse vibes dude.

#2540. Connor Hellebuyck trade: Jets send star goalie to the Devils in exchange for four players, two draft picks

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil. The star goalie for the Winnipeg Jets is on the move after being traded to New Jersey on Friday in exchange for four players and two future draft picks. the teams announced the move with the Jets receiving Dawson Mercer, Nick Bjugstad, Nico Daws and Alexander Command, plus a 2027 seventh-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.

Hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August. He said at the time that he had made the request months earlier and tried to keep the situation private.

Hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No. 130 overall. He's recognized as one of the best goalies in the league as a three-time Vezina Trophy winner. He also helped carry the United States to its first gold medal since 1980 at the 2026 Olympics in February with some incredible saves against Canada in the final game.

After trading Jacob Markstom in the offseason, the Devils had a clear need in goal, and this splashy move certainly fills that need. With a talented young core already in place, New Jersey's Stanley Cup window is wide open.

RAISE HELLE!Connor Hellebuyck is a New Jersey Devil: https://t.co/HCehRGOQI5 pic.twitter.com/dZGNQR16m1

For the Jets, it must be a hard pill to swallow when a franchise icon decides to walk out they door, but this trade package should help them as the enter a new era and revamp the roster. Winnipeg got a former first-rounder in Mercer to try and add to a rebuild as well as a veteran presence in Bjugstad. They also acquired a younger goalie in Daws who could fill the role of Hellebuyck at just 25 years old.

Goaltending has been an issue in New Jersey for a while now -- even after the team acquired Markstrom from the Calgary Flames in 2024. Markstom never really panned out, and his 13.6 goals allowed above average, per Natural Stat Trick, were a big reason why the Devils missed the postseason last year.

In the early portion of this season, it was clear that New Jersey needed to make a move to upgrade in the crease. Daws and veteran Jake Allen simply aren't a tandem suitable for a Stanley Cup contender, and the numbers backed that up. New Jersey ranks 24th in team save percentage at .877, and the duo of Daws and Allen combined to surrender 2.99 goals above average.

Once Hellebuyck gets up to game speed, that shouldn't be a problem anymore.

In the three-season stretch from 2023-26, Hellebuyck led the NHL with 73.42 goals saved above average, which is 20 goals higher than the next closest netminder. Over that span, Hellebuyck also posted a standard save percentage of .914 and an astronomical high-danger save-percentage of .832.

Hellebuyck carried less talented teams to the playoffs multiple times in his career. Now on a team loaded with weaponry in their prime -- Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt and Nico Hischier to name a few -- Hellebuyck could be the final piece to the championship puzzle.

In terms of the acquisition cost, it was probably an easy deal for Devils general manager Sunny Mehta to make. The 2029 second-round pick is useless for a team that should be all-in now, Bjugstad is simply a depth piece and Daws now has no path to a starting role with Hellebuyck in town.

The most interesting trade chips are Mercer and Command. Mercer flashed major upside with 56 points in his second NHL season, 2022-23, but he hasn't really come close to hitting those heights again. Still, even if he has plateaued, Mercer remains a strong middle-six forward rising into his prime.

Although Command had his detractors -- and may have been over-drafted at No. 12 overall -- he was a consensus first-round pick last summer. That gives Winnipeg a potential franchise forward it can build around long-term, but New Jersey already has one of the deepest forward groups in the league, especially with the emergence of Arseny Gritsyuk and the acquisition of Luke Evangelista.

If we're looking for a 3-D chess angle of this deal, it only makes the Devils more appealing for a certain Minnesota Wild defenseman whose brothers just happen to play in New Jersey already. Grade -- A+

Let's get the obvious out of the way first: The Jets were never going to get fair value for Hellebuyck because, at his best, he's the No. 1 goaltender in the world with no equal. That type of excellence can't be replaced.

That said, Winnipeg did fairly well given the circumstances. Hellebuyck made a public trade request, and he wasn't even with the team after sitting out for the entirety of training camp. The entire league knew the Jets had to trade him.

Hellebuyck's talent created a decent market anyway, but most of the suitors were bona fide Stanley Cup contenders with little in the way of valuable draft capital, and they weren't going to knee cap the roster by sending a key player back in return.

With all that taken into consideration, Kevin Cheveldayoff got a solid return. Although Mercer's ceiling may be lower than initially thought, he's a 24-year-old forward who banks roughly 20 goals and 20 assists every season. The kicker with Mercer will be Winnipeg's ability to re-sign him before he hits restricted free agency next summer.

The addition of Command means Winnipeg now has two forwards selected in the top 12 of the 2026 NHL Draft after taking center Viggo Bjorck themselves. If both of those players deliver on their first-round pedigrees, they could be a terrific one-two punch for the team long-term.

Daws was a third-round pick in 2020, and despite playing just 13 NHL games since the start of the 2024-25 season, he should give Winnipeg a solid back up option behind Stuart Skinner. It certainly helps that Skinner is off to a great start with his new team -- and if Daws develops into a true No. 1 -- it'll be gravy.

If there's any reason to critique this deal from the Jets' side of things, it's that they didn't get premium draft capital or a surefire up-and-coming prospect. Maybe Command develops into a star, but there's no guarantee he becomes a top-six stud in the NHL.

The Jets got a lot of good stuff, but they didn't really get anything great, at least not based on what we know in the moment. Because of that, I have to ding Winnipeg a little bit. Grade: B

#2539. MLB free agency: Six international players to know for the 2026-27 offseason

Major League Baseball's free agency period opened earlier this week and teams are now clear to pursue any roster upgrades they deem necessary. That includes players coming over from Japan's Nippon Professional Baseball league, South Korea's Korea Baseball Organization, and Taiwan's Chinese Professional Baseball League. Those are high-level leagues that have sent many impact players MLB's way over the years.

Look no farther than the Dodgers to see how important international talent can be to a club. The Dodgers employed four different former NPB and KBO players this past season, including two-way star Shohei Ohtani, ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto, and starter Roki Sasaki. Ohtani was signed as an MLB free agent, but the others went to the Dodgers through the posting system.

Per the posting agreement with MLB, posted NPB and CPBL players get a 45-day window to negotiate and sign with an MLB team. KBO players get a 30-day window. Players who do not sign during that posting window return to their previous team in NPB, CPBL, or KBO. The MLB team that signs a posted player pays a fee to the player's former NPB, CPBL, or KBO team.

$5M plus 17.5% of contract value over $25M

$9.375M plus 15% of contract value over $50M

For example, the White Sox paid Munetaka Murakami's former team, the Yakult Swallows, a $6.575 million posting fee on his $34 million contract last offseason. That's $5 million on the first $25 million plus 17.5% of the remaining $9 million, which is $1.575 million. The $5 million plus $1.575 million equals the $6.575 million posting fee paid to the Swallows.

Unlike last lockout, MLB will not be pausing the signing window during the expected lockout, according to The Athletic. In other words, if owners lock players out on Dec. 1 as expected, that date will essentially serve as the same deadline for already posted NPB players unless the lockout ends before their 45-day window expires.

There are no superstar-caliber players like Ohtani or Yamamoto available in this winter's international free agent crop. There are, however, several interesting players who can improve an MLB roster in 2027. Here are the six best NPB, CPBL, and KBO players to know this offseason.

Japan's Triple Crown winner hit .306/.383/.609 with 39 home runs in 2026. He has a similar skill set to Murakami but is not exactly Murakami 2.0. He doesn't have quite as much power (but has plenty of it) and won't walk nearly as often, but he does swing and miss a bunch and is unlikely to remain at the hot corner long-term. Sato is a very aggressive hitter who ran a 66% contact rate this past season. That is below the 77% MLB average. The consensus seems to be that he will land at first base or in a corner outfield spot if not next year, then soon. Murakami successfully overcame his contact issues to slug 35 homers in only 127 games in 2026 around a hamstring injury. At minimum, that will have MLB teams reconsidering how they evaluate the Japan-to-MLB transition. Like Murakami, Sato carries risk, and like Murakami, his power makes that risk worth the dice roll. The Hanshin Tigers officially posted Sato on Nov. 1.

Listed at 5-foot-8, Taira gets outlier extension down the mound (close to seven feet despite his height), which creates a low release window. Hitters rarely see the ball come from where Taira releases it. He's not a gimmick pitcher either. Taira sits mid-90s with his four-seam fastball and backs it up with a cutter, sinker, sweeper, slider, changeup, and splitter. The sweeper and slider are distinct pitches, as are the changeup and splitter. The Seibu Lions used Taira as a reliever in 2024 and 2025, then started him in 2026, and he handled the assignment well. The breaking balls are just OK, and the fact of the matter is that pitchers this height don't often hold up under a starter's workload. I would assume the team that signs Taira will give him a chance to start. In the long run, though, he might be a reliever, perhaps even a multi-inning setup man. Taira was officially posted on Nov. 1.

A down 2026 season took some of the shine off Itoh, who won the 2025 Eiji Sawamura Award (Japan's Cy Young equivalent) after throwing 196 ⅔ innings with a 2.52 ERA. To be sure, Itoh pitched well in 2026 (3.18 ERA in 172 ⅔ innings), but he was not as consistently dominant as in the past. The 5-foot-9 right-hander is a seven-pitch pitcher with a low-90s fastball and the usual array of secondary pitches (sinker, cutter, curveball, slider, sweeper, splitter), none of which stands out as a plus offering. Itoh has thrown at least 150 innings in each of the last six seasons. He's seen as a crafty back-end starter in MLB, or perhaps even a reliever (Itoh sat 96 mph out of the bullpen in the World Baseball Classic). The Hokkaido Nippon-Ham Fighters posted Itoh on Nov. 1.

Roh has an unusual agreement with the Hanwha Eagles. He signed the richest deal in KBO history in February (11 years and roughly $23 million), and as part of the deal, the Eagles agreed to post him for MLB teams this offseason, and Roh agreed to return to the Eagles to finish his career when his big-league stint is over. This past season, Roh, 26 in November, authored a .283/.360/.505 batting line with 29 home runs. He has real right-handed power and a good approach at the plate. There are concerns about his propensity to swing and miss as well as his arm at the hot corner. The Eagles formally posted Roh on Nov. 1.

The Seibu Lions posted Takahashi last offseason, but he was unable to find a contract to his liking, so he returned to Japan for another season and threw 148 innings with a 2.64 ERA. Takahashi, 30 in February, is an international free agent now, meaning he does not have to be posted and can instead negotiate at his own pace. More of a ground ball pitcher than a bat-misser, Takahashi sits in the 91-95 mph range with his fastball and has two good secondary pitches in his slider and splitter. He also throws a cutter and curveball. Takahashi is considered a potential innings guy for the back of an MLB rotation.

Tseng pitched for Chinese Taipei in the World Baseball Classic in 2023 and 2026 and he has been one of the CPBL's top relievers the last few years. In 2026, he saved 25 games with a 1.80 ERA and 65 strikeouts in 52 ⅓ innings. Tseng's fastball typically sits in the mid-90s and has run as high as 100 mph in the past, though it has been a few years. His go-to secondary pitch is a breaking ball that needs improvement for Tseng to carve out an MLB career as more than a middle reliever.

#2538. UNC-Louisville live updates: Score, highlights, predictions, analysis

After a convincing road win at UConn, the North Carolina Tar Heels return home to Chapel Hill for a high-stakes ACC football showdown.

On Saturday at 7 p.m. ET, UNC (5-4, 2-3 ACC) will host Louisville on a chilly, mid-November night. North Carolina needs one more win to become bowl eligible, while the Cardinals (6-3, 5-2 ACC), winners of four straight, are still in contention for the last conference championship game.

The last time your Tar Heels played Louisville, Lamar Jackson led his team 47-35 win back on September 9, 2017 in Chapel. UNC trails the all-time series, 5-3, last winning a matchup back in 2011 at home.

North Carolina quarterback Billy Edwards is playing his best football, leading one of the ACC's best offenses. Jelani Thurman and Jordan Shipp give the Tar Heels two dangerous pass-catchers, while their deep running back room forces opponents to pick their poison.

The Cardinals have one of the country's best dual-threat quarterbacks in Ohio State transfer Lincoln Keinholz, plus a Top-10 running back in Isaac Brown. Louisville's defense isn't great, while UNC's defense is fresh off its best performance of 2026.

Expect an offensive shootout in Chapel Hill tonight. Get real-time updates, scoring plays, turning points and expert analysis throughout UNC-Louisville. Follow along here for highlights, injury news, key plays and instant breakdown as the Tar Heels host the Cardinals in a high-stakes ACC showdown.

If you're a Waka Flocka Flame fan, he's today's Chapel Thrill pre-game concert.

UNC head coach Bill Belichick means business on his pre-game walk to Kenan Stadium. If the Tar Heels beat Louisville today, they clinch bowl eligibility in just Belichick's second year, a major reversal from an abysmal 2025.

Not only is tonight UNC's Military Appreciation Day, but also homecoming. Expect a packed Kenan Stadium.

ESPN's Jess Sims gave the UNC football team a shoutout on College GameDay this morning, recognizing the Tar Heels for hosting Military Appreciation Day in their 100th season at Kenan Stadium.

UNC — OUT: DB Tre Miller, LB Jonathan Agumadu, DL Joseph Mupoyi, DL Villami Moala, WR Kymistri Young, WR Keeyun Chapman, DL Vodney Cleveland, P Jacob Horvath; QUESTIONABLE: DL Emmanuel Nwaiwu; PROBABLE: DB Peyton Waters, TE Jelani Thurman, DL Jimmy-Phrisco Alo-Suliafu

Louisville — OUT: DB Antonio Watts, P Jacob Baker, OT Bryten Close, OL Anwar O'neal, WR Payton Cook, TE Hamilton Atkins, DL Sam Dawson; PROBABLE: RB Isaac Brown, DL Demeco Kennedy, WR Lawayne McCoy, DB Myles Norwood, OL Cason Henry

UNC 45, Louisville 41: Tonight will feature a matchup of two top offenses in the ACC. UNC has a variety of playmakers on its offense, while Louisville has one of the country's top QB-RB duos. North Carolina's defense came under fire during consecutive losses to Syracuse and Miami (FL), but responded emphatically vs. UConn. Louisville's defense allows over 400 yards per game, a mark the Tar Heels reached in consecutive contests. UNC finds a way to squeak out an upset win in a high-scoring shootout.

The forecast for Saturday night in Chapel Hill calls for 44 degrees and clear skies.

UNC vs. Louisville airs live on ESPN2 and will be streamed on WatchESPN and Fubo.

#2536. MLB rumors: Why the Dodgers could be Tarik Skubal or bust; Red Sox looking for pitching depth

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The biggest thing hanging over baseball this offseason is obviously the expiration of the CBA and what everyone assumes will be a lockout. Until then, we'll find out the major award winners this coming week, starting with Rookies of the Year on Monday. And, of course, there's the player movement yet to come.

For the latter, let's round up Sunday's rumors right here.

As we saw plenty in 2026, the Dodgers have a very talented rotation with a few injury-prone parts (Tyler Glasnow, Blake Snell, Shohei Ohtani as a pitcher, etc.). As such, this bit of speculative reporting from The Athletic makes a ton of sense:

The Dodgers will need someone who can cover innings in 2027. It's just a matter of how much they can lean on Justin Wrobleski, trust how Emmet Sheehan finished the season (I'd say probably a good amount), how healthy Gavin Stone is (unknown), how ready Jackson Ferris is (he seems close) and if they have enough depth options behind them.

All that to say, the Dodgers will be in on Skubal. If he goes elsewhere, I don't think it's as simple as the Dodgers going after the next highest-ranked starter on the market, such as a Freddy Peralta or a Michael King. I could see them taking a flier on some depth options to soak up innings in anticipation of a quick ramp-up post-lockout, sort of like they did when they signed Tyler Anderson in the run-up to the 2022 season.

Yes, the Dodgers are in on the Tarik Skubal bidding. We all know that. But if they lose out on retaining the two-time Cy Young winner, they may not just continue moving down the list for available starters. Then again, it's hard to ever know exactly what Andrew Friedman is going to spend money on.

As things stand, the Dodgers' rotation has Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Snell, Glasnow, Roki Sasaki and Sheehan, at least until Ohtani is ready to rejoin the fray.

Coming off two straight Wild Card Series losses and sub-90-win seasons, the Red Sox would surely like to take things up a notch for the 2027 season. One way might be to build out the depth of the pitching staff. They'll be "in the market for a back-end starter" and a right-handed reliever "with swing-and-miss capability," according to MassLive.

For the rotation: Sonny Gray hits free agency, but Garrett Crochet will return from a nearly full-season injury. Payton Tolle and Ranger Suárez fill the 2-3 spots, with Jake Bennett solid as the No. 4. That leaves Brayan Bello, Kutter Crawford and Tanner Houck as options for the fifth spot in addition to depth. It doesn't seem dire, but we've seen plenty of times what kind of havoc injuries can wreak.

In the bullpen, lefty Aroldis Chapman returns at closer with Garrett Whitlock and Erik Miller as setup men. Houck missing out on a rotation spot could mean he helps late as well.

#2535. The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly: Duke Blue Devils 2026 Edition

It was maybe a bit more fraught than we'd have liked, but Miami got back to their winning ways on Saturday afternoon with a 36-25 homecoming win over the Duke Blue Devils.

Craig T. Smith has your game recap, and Mike Schiffman has your 3 stars. Links below!

And now, let's dive into The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly

A win! Winning isn't easy, and I will never take it for granted, regardless of opponent.

QB Darian Mensah. The #HeisMensah campaign continues. 30/41 passing (73.2% completions) for 382 yards with 1 touchdown and 0 interceptions, 4 carries, 7 yards rushing.

Mensah's cumulative stats: 241/317 passing, 76.0% completions, 3,083 yards, 29 touchdowns, 2 interception, 39 carries, 144 yards, 2 touchdowns.

RB Javian Mallory. Mark Fletcher Jr. didn't play after halftime, and the superstar stepped up huge. 10 carries for 71 yards and 2 touchdowns, and 3 catches for 79 yards and a touchdown. Just a monster performance, with nearly all his yards and all 3 touchdowns coming in the 2nd half.

WR Cooper Barkate. 8 catches for 134 yards. Looked like the Barkate we saw at Duke last year…just AGAINST Duke this year.

RB Jordan Lyle. 7 carries for 54 yards. And, more importantly, he's starting to look like HIMSELF again, not this shell of a player we've seen for the last 25 games across 2 years. That's big for Miami moving forward.

WRs Daylyn Upshaw and Vandrevius Jacobs, and TE Elija Lofton all had 5+ catches as well, and solid (if imperfect) play.

S Dylan Dyan and JJ Dunnigan both had 6 tackles, and Dunnigan had a TFL. Again, solid if imperfect.

S Bryce Fitzgerald had 3 tackles, a TFL, and a PBU (but the latter should have been a pick-6. I still can't believe he dropped that).

EDGE Third Scroggins with one of the only pressures of the day. Great rush by him. Needs more snaps.

K Jake Weinberg. 3/3 on FGs, perfect on PATs, and good kickoffs. The one kickoff that was returned was because the kick came from our 20 after a penalty to end the previous drive. Not his fault.

P Dylan Joyce. 2 punts, 46 yard average. Ho hum.

Duke RB Nate Sheppard. He's so good, he's one of the few opposing players ever to make it here on The Good. But Duke's offense is a one-man band, and Sheppard is him. 16 carries for 131 yards and 2 touchdowns rushing, 12 catches for 93 yards receiving, and 2/2 passing (100% completions) for 16 yards. He did everything he could, and it was a tour de force performance. He's a Heisman finalist in my eyes. Incredible player. Bravo.

Nice coverage and PBU by Xavier Lucas on to end Duke's first drive. That's what I'm talking about, defense!

DBs Damari Brown, Xavier Lucas, and Ethan O'Connor playing through the whistle to get late PBUs on Duke's first few drives.

S J.J. Dunnigan with a solid tackle (for a loss even!) on a shallow crosser to end Duke's second possession.

EDGE Herbert "Third" Scroggins III with a nice rush move to get pressure on the play that ended with the Dunnigan TFL. Good to see someone start winning up front along the DL.

Touchdown, Mark Fletcher Jr! And with this run, he's now Miami's all-time leader in rushing touchdowns. He was already the all-time leader in total touchdowns, and extends that record with every score as well.

This 63 yard touchdown reception by Javian Mallory. The pass was very short, the run after catch was long and incredible. My goodness, 21 can hoop!

The Javian Mallory era is here. This 39 yard touchdown fully put the game out of reach. Elite.

73 plays (T-3rd most in a game this year)

11 chunk plays — 8 passes (15+), 3 runs (10+)

Advanced stats show a game with 61 total points, but one team being about 2 scores better. Which was what happened.

Settling for field goals. This should have been a 50+ burger easy.

The pass rush. If I can count a single Scroggins rep as the pass rush today, that's a bad thing. So, bad.

Some of the angles taken by defenders trying to make tackles. We're athletic, but contextually stupid. Situation, location, leverage. None seem to be considered when trying to stop the opposition, and I 'd like that to change.

The offensive line overall. Wild to say this in a game with 36 points and 500+ yards of offense….but true.

The blocking on this Barkate screen. This. Should. Have. Scored. There are 2 defenders and 3 OL leading the way and none of them touched a defender, allowing the tackle. Sure, it converted a 1st down, but this should have been a touchdown.

Specifically, Rodriguez, Woodrow, and Okunlola all missed blocks here. Fletcher was intentionally slowing down to allow for the running lane for Barkate behind the OL, so he's where the tackle occurred, but he didn't miss a block. Video below.

The refs giving Duke several free timeouts for reviews that were obvious calls the first time.

The refs THEN ruling a Duke player down when Miami's defense was contending they punched the ball out after a 4th down completion and recovered the fumble. And the refs let Duke go tempo to the line to run a play to negate any chance of a review. Really fucking cool. Great shit.

This Duke 47 yard touchdown run. Great for them, terrible for us.

Another Elija Lofton touchdown catch overturned on review. This one was clearly out of bounds, but the mugging for DPI that he endured and was uncalled is quite egregious, in my humble opinion.

Holding on the defense (look at the back of Wingo's jersey). Clear and obvious and uncalled.

4 TFLs. It's fine, but should have been more if not for missed tackles.

The pass rush. Seriously, it's at 5-alarm fire status now. 0 sacks yet again.

Allowed 130 yards rushing. 2nd worst number of the season, only behind the FSU game.

Allowed 7.6 yards per rush. Unacceptable, regardless of the RB on the opposing team.

Allowed 20 first downs, including several long disatance 3rd down conversions.

Allowed 5.6 yards per play. Needs to be lower than this.

Allowed 2/2 4th down conversions, including one for the final Duke touchdown of the game.

Allowed 3/3 red zone scoring — 2 TD, 1 FG

Allowed 7 chunk plays — 5 passes (15+), 2 runs (10+….and both went for exactly 47 yards lol)

10 penalties for 69 (not nice) yards. As per usual, I will be listing each one here in The Ugly.

Offsides with contact, Justin Scott. Gave Duke a 1st down on their initial 3rd down of the game.

Holding, SJ Alofaituli. On Miami's 1st offensive play. He was kinda hung out to dry because the quick pass concept wasn't thrown and Mensah held the ball………but still.

Holding, Cooper Barkate. Negated a nice Fletcher run.

The entire first offensive possession. Holding on the 1st play. Holding on another play. Referee stopped a play to re-spot the ball THAT THEY'D JUST SPOTTED. Snapped it 5 times, but go 3-and-out with the penalties. The definition of Ugly.

False star, SJ Alofailtuli. Turned 2nd and 3 into 2nd and 8 in the red zone.

Miami settling for a pair of field goals after reaching the red zone. Need 7's.

True Freshman LG Ben Congdon getting manhandled on 3rd and goal for a sack before the final FG of the first half.

Oh joy! That was actually a sack on a 3 man rush. Terrific!

Allowing a 4 yard checkdown on 3rd and 18 convert. That's piss poor.

Missed a sack AND an interception (likely pick-6) on the same play. Weeeee!

This is absolutely targeting with the crown of the helmet by the Duke. Refs refused to call it.

After the failed 2pt play, unsportsmanlike conduct, Elija Lofton.

This might be the softest penalty I've ever seen. Duke player flopped like a fish from the lightest of touches by Lofton to get him up off of Mensah. SMH.

The ensuing kickoff came from the Miami 20. Duke returned it to their 35, and scored 5 plays and 1:56 later. Direct correlation to the above penalty.

A HORRIBLE missed tackle by Ethan O'Connoor on Duke star RB Nate Sheppard. Ball was caught at about 4 yards, but O'Connor whiffed the play BADLY and let Sheppard run for 20. Unacceptable.

Duke's QB lateral'd the ball to Sheppard, and it bounced off him for a fumble. Replay overturned it based on nothing. Total bullshit.

Pass interference, Ethan O'Connor. More ref bullshit. Fuck this guy, man.

Illegal substitution, defense. Too many men on the field. Half the distance to the 2 yard line, 2nd and goal.

Offsides, Dylan Day. Half the distance. 3rd and goal on the 1.

Offsides, defense (player unspecified). Half the distance. 4th and goal inside the 1.

The counting numbers for yards got real big, and the points got to a nice place, but Miami left tons of meat on the bone and points on the field today. This should have been a 50 burger easy. Settling for 3 FGs, dropping a pick-6 (not on the offense, but still matters to the point total), some bad OL play, and a passing game that was effective but lacked explosion are all factors affecting this grade. On the flip side, 36 points 532 yards and a win on homecoming over a team looking for revenge on multiple levels who had just won their previous 2 games by a combined score of 88-5 is pretty damn good. Still, we'll need to be better to accomplish our goals, so this is the grade.

Look. Nate Sheppard is good, but he's a 1 man team. Allowing him to go crazy the way we did/he did is just bad. Holding Duke to 4 scores on 9 offensive possessions is good, but I'd like that number to be lower. Miami was robbed of a turnover on one drive where the player who fumbled didn't even try to say he didn't, but the refs gave Duke the ball, and the Blue Devils went with tempo so there was no chance for a review. If that, and the last touchdown, come off the board, I'd have felt better with 10-13 points allowed being the result. But it wasn't. So I have to grade what happened. And I did.

3/3 FGs. Great punts. Good coverage. The only thing keeping this from being an A was the long KR on the kickoff from the 20 after the Lofton Unsportsmanlike penalty. When given room, opposing returners and return teams continually crease Miami's kick coverage unit. I don't like it. Oh, and the hands team for the final kickoff was prepared for an onside kick, and the returner (Fitzgerald) fielded the squibbed kick flawlessly to possess the ball and allow Miami to go with Victory Formation. MUCH better here.

There were good moments and bad moments, but overall I think this was a strong showing. The coaches had the team dialed in and ready to compete, looking to bounce back from the Notre Dame loss. There was some lethargy early, and the offense took a while to get going, but the defense got 3 straight punts to start the game, so that's good! The big thing here with the demerit were the penalties and lack of performance from the players. At a certain point, guys just need to make plays. That's on the players, not the coaches. So for those who are reading this and thinking "OMG Shannon Dawson is stupid", consider that for like the 6th game out of 10 this year, Miami had a penalty before the first offensive snap of the game. And consider, if you will, that he's not calling plays with the intent of OL whiffing blocks. AND, also consider that Corey Hetherman is not designing his defense to intentionally and continually miss tackles. So, I say that to say that, coming off the Notre Dame loss, on Homecoming, at Noon, against a team that'd just won consecutive games by an aggregate 88-5, with a program whose coach and multiple staffers have personal grudges against Miami, this was a solid performance and 2 score win. I'll take it.

That's it for this installment of The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly.

Hop in the comments and share your thoughts.

#2532. MLB rumors: Why the Cubs may already be out on Tarik Skubal, plus latest on Phillies, Cardinals, more

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway. The ongoing CBA negotiations and the near certainty of an owner-implemented lockout on Dec. 2 loom over all, and it may indeed mean a flurry of trades and free agent signings leading up to that date. That was certainly the case leading up to the last lockout of 2021-22.

Thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace, offseason rumors are already flowing. Speaking of which, we'll be here each day to round up what's out there. You can find Monday's supply just below.

The expectation remains that we'll see some level of activity on the trade and free agency fronts before the lockout begins in early December. As noted above, that was indeed the case leading up to the last lockout, and this time around, the prospect of drastic changes in the next CBA may have big-spending teams looking to fortify their rosters before those changes are implemented. Speaking of which, MLB Network reports that we could see some notable transactions go down at the upcoming General Managers Meetings, which take place from Nov. 10-12 in Las Vegas.

During a standard offseason, not much beyond behind-the-scenes groundwork goes down during the GM Meetings, and the real moves start happening at the December Winter Meetings. However, unless the lockout is resolved quickly – highly unlikely – then there probably won't be a Winter Meetings this offseason. That means the GM Meetings could be more active than usual.

Free agent ace and, until later this week, reigning back-to-back  American League Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal is the prize of the offseason. The 29-year-old lefty is a fit for any of MLB's 30 teams, but heretofore the most serious bidders have been expected to be the Los Angeles Dodgers (who acquired Skubal from the Detroit Tigers leading up to last season's trade deadline), the New York Mets, and the Chicago Cubs. Now, though, perhaps you can reduce that number of serious bidders to two. While Chicago very much needs rotation help for 2027 and beyond, the Athletic reports that the Cubs "are expected to stay on the sidelines" when the Skubal bidding gets serious. That, no doubt, will come as a disappointment to Cubs fans who are still waiting for the Ricketts to invest in the payroll at levels befitting a big-market contender.

The Cardinals traded away veteran lefty reliever JoJo Romero, along with starter and fellow free agent Dustin May, to the Milwaukee Brewers leading up to the trade deadline. Now, St. Louis may be interested in bringing Romero back on a free agent contract, the St. Louis Post-Dispatch reports.

Romero, 30, is coming off a 2026 season in which he pitched to a 3.36 ERA with a 3.00 K/BB ratio in 55 appearances. In the postseason with Milwaukee, Romero had a 1.13 ERA with 11 strikeouts and one walk in eight innings. He previously spent parts of five seasons with the Cardinals.

Do the Philadelphia Phillies need a new shortstop? That's one of the principal questions of their offseason. Although incumbent Trea Turner is signed through 2033, his defense at the crucial position of shortstop has degraded into "unplayable" territory, and that has the Phils considering fallback options should Turner need to be moved off the position. One option is free agent 31-year-old Ha-Seong Kim, NBC Sports Philadelphia reports. Kim, 32, spent last season on a one-year deal with the division-rival Atlanta Braves. He's been a primary shortstop for five of his six MLB seasons, and while he's certainly not among the very best at the position, he does profile as a major defensive upgrade over Turner. As for the bat, Kim for his career has an OPS+ of 93, and he's capable of stealing a base on occasion. He was, however, an offensive sinkhole for 51 games in 2026. Turner, meantime, may be looking at a switch to the outfield starting next season as the Phillies attempt to keep their contending window open.
